Despite having an online mode that disappoints in nearly every respect, Smash Bros Brawl gets everything else right.

The questions you need to ask yourself before deciding to invest in Super Smash Bros. Brawl concern your own personal level of love for Nintendo’s rich history and your ability to rustle up enough enthusiastic locals to get into the multiplayer…
Perhaps by being willing to limit itself, Brawl could have been a great game. As it stands, it is simply the strongest iteration of a great series.

Nintendo's third entry in the Smash Bros series isn't just a trip down nostalgia lane - it's also a heck of a fun experience. With an insane amount of content and a gameplay begging for sessions with a bunch of friends this is a perfect addition to the series…

If you've got a few like minded friends to play with you, this is some of the best fun you can have with your Wii yet. Single players will be left scratching their heads wondering what the hubbub is really all about.

It's certainly a game that can kill a bit of time between a group of friends, and it's not like there'll be many negative memories associated with the game afterwards, but I just don't feel it's that good.
I started playing one afternoon and didn’t stop for nine hours. The interlocking systems, the pleasing pace, the ebb and flow between Olympus and the mortal realm are almost hypnotic…
Mythmatch is absolutely delightful. I was so absorbed playing that I lost many hours excitedly giving in to “just one more in-game day”…
Mythmatch brought a breath of life back to the merge genre and offers a variety of things to do, whether it be in the growing city of Ithaca or up in Olympus.
It's a process as intuitive and satisfying as any merge-based puzzler... [Issue#422, p.121]
Mythmatch twists expectations of what a match-3 game can be with an excellent narrative with fun characters and clever gameplay.
An odd mix of classic Match 3 puzzling, adventure, and mythology that works if you’re patient, but that also made a few key decisions that are more aggravating than they should be
Mythmatch merges Greek mythology into a colourful match-3 town-building game. Its witty, well-scripted, and satirical take on the Greek gods and corporate workplaces made me laugh…
At its core, MythMatch combines match-three mechanics, crafting, and light puzzle-solving into a gameplay loop that is immediately accessible and easy to settle into.

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is a fantastic conclusion to Estelle and Joshua's chapters in the Sky series. The story is fantastic, with fantastic reunions and dark moments that really stay with the player…

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter picks up everything 1st Chapter introduced and improves upon it. It features outstanding combat, an impeccable narrative, and a captivating cast, while cutting the slow-burn segments of the first game…
Building upon the already excellent work done in the remake of the first game, Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is a masterclass in how to make a JRPG…

Building on the already-great remake of the first game, Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter masterfully updates the gameplay and timeless story, adding up to what is now the Trails series’ defining entry, and one of the best RPGs of the year.

Another swing and another home run for GungHo. Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is another stellar remake that provides plenty of quality of life improvements over the first game but also tells a fantastic story with plenty of added cutscenes and fantastic voice work…

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is a masterful remake that elevates an already beloved RPG with stronger presentation, refined combat, meaningful quality-of-life improvements, and excellent character work…

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is the payoff 1st Chapter was building toward. The dungeons and backtracking keep it just short of perfect, but the storytelling and presentation are as good as RPGs get right now.

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is the excellent sequel to the first game, which serves as an introduction to everything that's to come in one of the most massive JRPG sagas—and it masterfully demonstrates how to create a remake…
Can you enjoy this remake if you’ve already played through SC? I can wholeheartedly say yes, as replaying the story again illuminated some plot points for me in ways I hadn’t expected…

Building on the remake expertise of the first game, Trails in the Sky the 2nd is a masterclass in modernizing a classic. With snappier pacing, deeper turn-based combat, and dynamic direction that easily overshadows modest visuals, it effortlessly hooks you for a relentless 20-plus-hour ride.
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter captures everything that made the original so endearing while giving it an impressive makeover that enhances its elegant storytelling and charismatic cast.

Direct sequels simply don't get much better than Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter. With its already excellent predecessor setting the stage, this brilliantly heartfelt RPG is free to tell an outstanding character-driven story.
Trails in the Sky Second Chapter is a superb sequel that builds meaningfully on its predecessor while modernizing one of the series’ most beloved adventures.

While 1st Chapter laid the foundations of Trails in a modernized form, Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter gives the journey its full depth, delivering a title that is more ambitious, darker, and even more expansive.

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is a spectacular remake that mirrors a lot of the merits that its predecessor brought to the table. It supplies stellar performance and visuals, a great story and soundtrack, and an addictive, depth-filled combat system that keeps you engaged from start to finish…
The name gives it away; this feels more like the second part of a larger game than a full follow-up, which is why we’re getting it only a year after the first part…

Sequels are supposed to do everything bigger and better. Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter definitely finds a way to continuously up the ante, with compelling story arcs for every character that keep the player glued to the screen…

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is such an excellent RPG follow-up so if you played and enjoyed the first remake, you're bound to fall in love with this freshly remade sequel in all of its characterful good times.

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is a sequel that builds on everything done right in 1st Chapter, maintaining quality across the board. It might play it safe, but perhaps that is its greatest strength: not fixing what wasn't broken…
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is a beautiful remake with an amazing story, a great ensemble cast, fun combat, and a killer soundtrack that deserves mainstream attention.

Trails in the Sky: 2nd Chapter is a darn fine RPG and exactly what its title promises: the second half of a two-part game. It doesn't try to reinvent the formula, and its modest combat additions don't substantially change the experience…

With Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter, Falcom brilliantly concludes the remake of the initial Trails saga. More than just a sequel, this second part builds upon all the strengths of the original to deliver a memorable finale…
The second installment in Nihon Falcom’s *Trails in the Sky* remake project once again delivers an outstanding performance…

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter proves that a good sequel doesn't need to reinvent everything that worked in its predecessor. Falcom sticks to the formula, delves deeper into its characters, and expands on a story that needed this second installment to feel complete…
A great continuation with one of the best casts and combat systems in a JRPG…
This remake of Trails’ second chapter does everything the great 1st Chapter does, but waits almost 40 hours before doing any of it in an inventive or engaging way…
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter continues the saga of Estelle Bright in an epic RPG adventure.

Trails in the Sky: 2nd Chapter is more of the same, and that is definitely a good thing. It's part of an exemplary remake cycle that rivals Final Fantasy VII's.The new adventure takes us back through familiar areas while continuing the journey of Estelle and Joshua Bright…

They’re massive storytelling endeavors that are always compelling in their ambition and earnestness, with a massive cast of characters who are a joy to spend time with. Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is very much an iterative sequel to the first remake, and that’s all it really needed to be.
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is an excellent remake that successfully modernizes Falcom's classic JRPG without compromising its stellar narrative…

While my love for the Trails series is well documented at this point, it was back when I completed the original Trails in the Sky SC that it became a full-on obsession. To see such an important game to me, remade with such love and care warms my heart…
All in all, Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is a great update to a legendary title. I had a great time plunging back into Liberl, and I think you will, too.
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is a phenomenal game, but places so much focus on its story that the gameplay can occasionally feel like an afterthought.
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter continues its winning streak with excellent storytelling, robust and fluid hybrid action/turn-based combat, and jaw-dropping music and environmental design.
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is the Trails series at its peak. Refined gameplay, better-balanced party systems, an amazing story, and huge character depth make this a must-play title.
Without a doubt, Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter successfully makes the series great again today, cementing its place as one of the most essential JRPGs of the year…
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is just as good as its predecessor, maybe even better. If you love the JRPG genre, you simply must play it…

Trails in the Sky Chapter 2 has prepared an incredible feast for fans of the series and has become the best Trails game to date. Especially if you consider both games as a package, you will probably have witnessed one of the best adventures in history.

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is a significantly bigger video game than its predecessor, so if you're open to an RPG that can easily take 60-100 hours, you'll find one here that's worthy of your time…

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is an act of love toward a way of understanding role-playing games that many thought was lost. It is a colossal work, the child of old-school writing that is not afraid to take its time to introduce characters and accompany them through wonderful coming-of-age stories…
Repeating success after a masterpiece is always hard, but with this game Nihom Falcom has made it look easy…
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is one of the best games of 2026, but it risks being overlooked for being simply a remake of a niche title, best known among JRPG fans.
This is best enjoyed as it was designed, as a follow-up to The Legend of Heroes: Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter.

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter builds on an already captivating story, further showcasing the series’ memorable characters and world-building. Despite its slow pacing and some repetitive elements, the remake delivers an emotional adventure with engaging combat and a memorable soundtrack…
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter successfully modernizes a beloved JRPG without losing what made the original special…

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter builds on its excellent predecessor with stronger character development, more engaging battles, and a more emotional story. Familiar environments and minor gameplay frustrations do little to diminish this outstanding RPG sequel.
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is an incredible remake that adapts the original sequel into a vibrant and refreshing game…
The Legend of Heroes: Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter does everything the 1st Chapter does right and is just as incredible and essential.
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition is yet another excellent remake in the Trails franchise…

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter takes a beloved story and modernizes it almost perfectly, implementing solid combat mechanics—though the pacing stumbles slightly—while remaining thoroughly enjoyable. The result is a phenomenal RPG featuring some of the best storytelling and characters in the genre…

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is an outstanding JRPG remake that delivers a deeply emotional, character-driven story, exceptional world-building, and a refined combat system blending real-time action with tactical turn-based battles…

Two games in, this remake is making a very strong case for why Trails in the Sky deserves to be revisited. The story and characters remain the heart of Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter, and the new presentation makes Liberl feel more alive than ever…
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is another masterful remake that brings the classic game to a new audience with its brilliant storytelling, excellent gameplay loop, and wonderful visuals…

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is one of the best JRPGs of 2026 and as a must-play title for fans of Nihon Falcom’s game series. Players will find a deep story filled with endearing, well-developed characters and an excellent evolution of the hybrid combat system…
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter picks up directly where the climactic ending of the first chapter left off. Estelle is once again on Joshua’s trail and continues her fight against the evil Ouroboros…
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is a remarkable JRPG remake that expands upon its predecessor with a deeper story, more freedom to explore Liberl and an improved combat system…
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is a truly outstanding JRPG, capable of transforming a story already beloved for years into a modern, intense, and deeply satisfying experience.
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter builds impressively on the foundations of 1st Chapter, with a much more ambitious story, stronger character development, and memorable twists…
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter maintains the high standard of excellence set by the first game, bringing Estelle and Joshua’s journey as protagonists of the Trails franchise to a conclusion…
There isn't much to say about Trail in the Sky 2nd Chapter, other than how special it is. One of the best stories in JRPGs has now been modernized and is available to the whole world…
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter blends heartfelt storytelling, memorable characters, tactical combat, and modern visuals into a rewarding JRPG.
Trails in the Sky: 2nd Chapter expands its predecessor with richer world-building, stronger character development, and deeper combat customisation…
This is how you do a Remaster! The newly added hybrid combat mechanics are as brilliant as the classic Quartz systems…
This second installment maintains the same quality as the first remake released by Falcom, featuring a story as moving as few others and impressive graphics…
Deeper and far more complete, Trails in the Sky: Second Chapter is highly recommended for those who played the first game…
Nihon’s faithful remake captures the essence of what made the original title a classic, while embracing modern gameplay elements that—we hope—will cater to new audiences

The task of remaking one of the greatest games of all time is a hefty one that most developers would be wise to avoid trying. Despite that, Falcom has put their best foot forward an delivered a near-perfect game that is sure to please any fan of the RPG genre, be they hardcore or casual…
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter brings one of the most beloved stories in the Trails series to a modern stage and also surpasses the already high bar that its predecessor left last year.

Nihon Falcom has delivered a remake that strikes the perfect balance of maintaining the iconic spirit of the original for the existing fans while updating the game with 3D visuals and full voice acting to bring in new fans with a much more modern experience.

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter delivered what its fans were waiting for; it presented a heartwarming story, vast content, amazing characters, enjoyable combat, and an exciting progression system, thereby delivering a well-rounded experience from various aspects…
Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter’s highs are nothing short of incredible. Once Estelle and company got going, the game never stopped giving and it never stopped letting up…

With a meatier amount of content and the impressive visuals that made the 1st Chapter stand out, Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter delivers a more solidified RPG experience that’s worth picking up. Exploration is fun, and I keep coming back for more…

Given that the game is a direct continuation and has you explore most of the same areas, the fact that its gameplay systems keep things fresh makes it all the more impressive, and that goes without saying the game is roughly one and a half times bigger than the last one…

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter, RPG fans, is yet another excellent remake of this magical saga that I enjoy so much. The game turned out really cool, and I believe it reinforces the point that remaking these classic games was indeed the right choice.

Second Chapter did everything it needed to do, and more. While the game doesn't refine or add new combat mechanics, the story and character moments that take place in this follow-up are some of the best of the series.
Like 1st Chapter, Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter is a remake made by a team that clearly shows love and reverence for the original game, and genuinely enjoyed making it…

Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter proves that a great story can remain powerful even when you already know how it ends. Rather than simply placing a classic narrative on top of modern visuals and systems, the remake carefully reworks its gameplay to fit the setting and technological level of its era…
An excellent choice for longtime fans of the Trails series, returning players who have already experienced the original, and newcomers looking to take their first step into the series…

A second remake that surpasses the memories of the original has been introduced. Estelle's journey to thwart the Society's conspiracy and find Joshua is depicted in a manner befitting the year 2026, perfectly conveying the emotional resonance of the original game along the way…

dave-the-diver-in-the-jungle.title: Dave the Diver: In the Jungle

reviews.excerpt: Dave the Diver is a fantastic game, and In the Jungle is every bit as good. The quality and variety on offer are something few games can match.
What stands out most is how natural all of it feels. Utara Village feels like it has always been part of Dave’s world…
Dave the Diver In the Jungle is a fantastic DLC that could be sold as a game in its own right, and is packed full of new ideas and jungle charm.
Mintrocket have advertised the In the Jungle DLC as the largest and most ambitious DLC for Dave the Diver yet; a huge celebration of the title's third birthday…
Like Bancho's cooking, Dave's new adventure is delicious.
Drei Jahre nach dem Überraschungserfolg Dave the Diver schickt euch der In the Jungle-DLC auf eine neue Insel mit frischen Fischen, einem neuen Restaurant und jeder Menge Nebenbeschäftigungen.
As a longtime farming and life sim enthusiast, I felt right at home, but I could see some fans yearning for simpler times…
For those fans who’ve been waiting for the next Dave the Diver, this DLC more than bridges a gap. It arrives as a near full-length sequel to its predecessor, at just a fraction of the cost…

In the Jungle is a phenomenal expansion for Dave the Diver, the wildly entertaining game from Mintrocket that has been a huge hit since its release in 2023. Our favorite diver faces a new setting and a slew of exciting minigames, ranging from rhythm games to JRPG-style turn-based combat…
A no-brainer for Dave the Diver fans, the new In the Jungle DLC is well worth diving into.

An expansion that could almost pass as a brand-new game. The core diving loop is enriched by a Stardew Valley-esque village, JRPG-style jungle exploration, and a mountain of new activities delivered with charming levity…

Dave the Diver: In the Jungle is definitely a must-have DLC. It feels like the perfect way to continue the Dave the Diver saga, and the addition of a plethora of content makes it worth the price tag and the time commitment…
Dave the Diver: In the Jungle is a content-packed DLC. Although it leaves the Blue Hole behind for the jungle, the core charm and strengths of Dave the Diver remain intact…

The same magical, carefree spirit that makes the artistic side of In the Jungle so appealing carries over into the gameplay, with the difference that Bancho’s fishing and sushi bar have received further enhancements compared to the past.
Dave the Diver: In the Jungle successfully carries over the enjoyable loop of exploration and restaurant management, offering a fresh experience in its new setting…

Despite primarily being a diver, Dave managed to hold his own quite well on dry land. Although the expansion lacks the same spark of originality that the base game brought at launch, it was a good idea to use the reduced scope to promote certain gameplay experiments.
In the Jungle transforms Dave the Diver and breathes new life into him. This DLC is so extensive that it's practically a spin-off…
Despite making waves in the gameplay department, Dave the Diver’s In the Jungle DLC presents a problematic narrative premise that blemishes everything it touches.
Dave the Diver's latest DLC – the biggest yet – is a true triumph. It adds so much to the base game, it plays more like a sequel…
There’s more to Dave the Diver than wasting away between the sea and sushi shop. In the Jungle is a meaningful expansion of the Dave the Diver-verse…
In The Jungle DLC delivers an ambitious new adventure packed with fresh discoveries, memorable moments, and enough content to feel like a sequel

"In the Jungle" is the ideal expansion for those who fell in love with Dave the Diver. With an interesting story, new mechanics, and packed with references to other games, the title shows that Mintrocket's creativity truly knows no bounds…

Dave the Diver In the Jungle pushes the bar higher by moving Dave into a completely new ecosystem, introducing fresh progression systems, expanding restaurant management, and adding a surprisingly engaging village life simulator…

For fans of *Dave the Diver*, *In the Jungle* is a must-buy: lovingly crafted, surprisingly substantial, and bold enough to meaningfully expand upon familiar mechanics rather than simply repeating them…
In the Jungle brings expansion-level volumes of new content, reigniting the same excitement first felt with Dave the Diver — a beautifully crafted DLC packed with everything fans love.
Dave the Diver: In the Jungle offers more of what made the original game so enjoyable, while once again finding ways to keep the experience feeling fresh…
"In the Jungle" does not attempt to alter the *Dave the Diver* formula but rather expand upon it with a new setting that refreshes the experience without compromising its essence…
This Jungle DLC is a shoo-in and, just like the base game, is a must-play. Loads of content and brilliant characters ensure yet more hours of gaming fun in Dave The Diver…
Dave the Diver: In the Jungle functions more like a substantial half-sequel than simple DLC, cleverly consolidating its core loop into an efficient central hub.
Perhaps one of the best DLCs (at least for a smaller "indie" game) I've played. Not only do you get more of an already great game, but they also give you multiple new gameplay elements…
This is a must-play for every fan of the series. The developers clearly show what a proper full-fledged DLC should look like, delivering 10 to 15 hours of honest fun for a ridiculously low price.

Dave the Diver: In the Jungle delivers somewhere between 10 and 15 hours of new content. A real story arc with an actual emotional payoff by the end, new mechanics in nearly every direction you look, and a price tag that doesn't ask much for everything you're getting…
Dave the Diver: In the Jungle is a fantastic DLC to this fun and addictive. With the new mechanics that kept being added and me enjoying the new things that appear…
Dave the Diver: In the Jungle is not just a simple addition to the original package, but a dazzling declaration of love from Mintrocket toward its own creation…
Numa era na qual muitas produtoras nem sequer se esforçam na tentativa de pedir mais dinheiro ao mesmo jogador, a corea…

In the Jungle shows what a successful expansion should look like. For a relatively modest amount, you don't get a handful of extra missions, but a substantial new adventure that effortlessly builds upon everything that made Dave the Diver so strong…

In the Jungle is a bold DLC, but also somewhat uneven. Mintrocket hasn't just offered more fish, more recipes, and more missions; it has created an expansion that transforms the structure of the base game…
In the Jungle is a massive add-on that feels more like a sequel than a DLC. This is one of the best Dave the Diver DLCs yet…
The biggest expansion yet for globally popular Dave the Diver trades the Blue Hole for a jungle lake and somehow ends up feeling like a sequel rather than a DLC.
Dave the Diver: In the Jungle is proof that Mintrocket understood exactly what makes their game special and decided to double down without betraying its essence…
I'll state the obvious first: If you enjoyed Dave the Diver, you'll enjoy this DLC. While the basic structure is "more of the same," the mechanics remain solid and fun…
Dave the Diver: In the Jungle is exactly the kind of expansion that many studios try to produce and few manage to deliver. It doesn't seek to reinvent what already worked…
From start to finish, Mina the Hollower had me enthralled, which is pretty incredible for a game that ran me about 18 hours for a first-time playthrough (54% exploration rating)…
Mina the Hollower is a brilliant 2D action-adventure game that takes clear inspiration from classic Zelda while building something that feels fresh, challenging, and uniquely its own…
More than just an ode to the GameBoy Color, Mina the Hollower is a masterclass in how constraints can fuel creativity. Inventive and engaging to the end and beyond, this is an instant modern classic…

Mina the Hollower is a rewarding journey all the way to the finish, and thanks to the extensive modifiers and also New Game+, I expect I'll have a blast seeing what we can do with this magnificently spooky adventure for a long time.

What is perhaps most impressive about Mina the Hollower is how effortlessly confident it feels. Many retro-inspired games are content to imitate the aesthetics of the past while sanding away the rougher edges…
A big game in a small package, and an absolute masterpiece of an adventure.

While Mina the Hollower might not play like the games it's clearly inspired by, Yacht Club Games has instead taken bits and pieces from all of its inspiration and combined it with its years of experience on Shovel Knight to create a masterpiece…

Mina the Hollower is an almost faultless game that combines elements of nostalgic classics we know and love with a healthy dose of Yacht Club’s flair and expertise to make it something that truly stands out as a retro-inspired masterpiece…

Best of all, Mina the Hollower is no mere nostalgia bait, proving the player-first design ethos evident in Yacht Club Games' past successes. As much as I love the Blue Burrower, I'm truly grateful that the studio took the risk of this new character and setting and followed it through…

With Mina the Hollower, Yacht Club Games managed to beautifully pay homage to some of the absolute greatest classics in gaming history, all while carving out their own entirely fresh identity with an irresistible experience…

Mina the Hollower is another masterpiece from Yacht Club Games, a Zelda style game that manages not only to equal the series that inspired it, but in some ways surpasses it. The world is detailed, gorgeous, and overflowing with secrets…

Mina the Hollower is an amazing title from Yacht Club Games that everyone needs to try. It looks and sounds spectacular, has awesome accessibility options, and is compelling to play; add this to your library right now.
Mina the Hollower is another practically perfect experience from Yacht Club Games, with retro challenge and a whole lot of creativity to show off.
Mina the Hollower doesn’t only trade in nostalgia; it’s a game that could only have been made today. But if you’re looking for vintage Sega or Nintendo-alike magic, here it is…
Almost a full decade on from Shovel Knight, Yacht Club Games has returned in full form…
Mina the Hollower is a masterfully crafted action adventure that confidently exceeds the towering expectations surrounding Yacht Club Games’ long-awaited follow-up to Shovel Knight…
With Mina the Hollower, Yacht Club Games captured lightning in a bottle a second time. It’s a must play experience.

Mina the Hollower feels like the result of a studio completely confident in its abilities. Its exceptional movement mechanics, rewarding exploration, challenging combat, and dense world design constantly make discovery feel exciting…
Mina the Hollower is simply a blast to play and is another success by Yacht Club Games that will make anyone who plays it ask for more of this darker world they’ve created.
Mina the Hollower is one of the best and most challenging games to come out in 2026. It brings great level design, balanced backend gameplay, and delivers plenty of ways to enjoy it.
Mina The Hollower is the Skill Issue of video games. Developer Yacht Club is not here to hold your hand…

Mina the Hollower is a grand, exhilarating adventure that never lets up, springing out fully formed as an absolute "mouse-terpiece." The thrill of discovering new areas, levelling Mina up to become stronger, and conquering seemingly impossible boss fights only gets more rewarding as you utilize…
Mina the Hollower possesses the allure of video games that are unafraid to ask something of the player: attention, memory, curiosity, and a certain tolerance for defeat…

Mina the Hollower is an action RPG that takes the best of Zelda, Castlevania and the Soulslike genre without ever feeling like a copy. Yacht Club Games builds a dense, challenging, incredibly smart and personality-driven adventure, capable of turning every screen into a continuous discovery.

Mina the Hollower proves that time, effort, and attention to some of the smallest details goes a long way. Mina is a great new hero that controls incredibly well in a difficult but rewarding 2D adventure.

Mina the Hollower easily cements Yacht Club Games' capacity to deliver high-quality retro experiences. The game takes inspiration from several sources, both old and new, and carefully fine-tunes each into a polished experience that is both curated and customizable.
An uncommon tribute to classic games that often surpasses the quality of the titles that inspired it

Mina the Hollower is a challenging game with memorable bosses and enemies, numerous secrets, and several interesting systems. The difficulty can be a bit unbalanced at times, but this doesn't detract from the excellent work that Yacht Club Games has delivered.
Mina the Hollower combines strong exploration, tight combat, and a fantastic retro presentation into an atmospheric action-adventure game packed with secrets and personality…
Mina the Hollower was well worth the wait. It gives you all the vibes of the best old-school games, while bringing its own modern sensibilities with smartly paced exploration and tight gameplay…

Mina the Hollower does for Zelda what Shovel Knight did for Mega Man. It's a revival of a classic franchise in spirit while having enough of its own flavor and style to avoid coming across as a simple clone or copy…

The game admirably captures the classic Game Boy essence, adapting it to the modern era with a fascinating and whimsical world to get lost in. Yacht Club Games achieves excellence once again with Mina the Hollower, a creative title that stands out for its exquisite gameplay and constant innovation.
Mina the Hollower therefore never feels like a cheap attempt to ride the simple wave of nostalgia. It isn't just another game in an ocean full of new-old indie titles with tacked-on retro graphics…

A worthy spiritual successor to Yacht Club Games’ Shovel Knight series, Mina the Hollower takes the studio’s love of retro aesthetics and strange fascination with digging and has crafted a fantastic world to explore, above and below ground…

Mina the Hollower is an incredible action adventure game that manages to offer a lot to explore and significant depth in its combat and exploration mechanics. Every single time you try to see just a little more, and you can open up many new possibilities with new items and game-changing features…
Mina the Hollower emerges as a new instant classic from Yacht Club Games, delivering a charming adventure in a punishing yet extremely satisfying world to explore…

Yacht Club Games stated that, for them, Mina is an all-or-nothing proposition: if it doesn't sell well, the studio goes under. And, honestly—given that quality and that launch price—I feel the same way…

Mina the Hollower is a retro dungeon adventure, which takes its inspiration from classic Game Boy titles and horror tales with a Victorian setting. A solid selection of gear and upgrades, modern gameplay mechanics and soulslike elements give this game a modern touch…
Mina the Hollower delivers expansive exploration, a world full of personality, and a constant sense of discovery through its varied situations and inventive systems…
I am awed by what Yacht Club Games has created here. Mina the Hollower is so ambitious and dense and sprawling that it is hard to believe that it is contained in such a modest presentation…

The fact that I enjoyed Mina The Hollower as much as I did despite its few playability shortcomings and the fact that I'm not necessarily familiar with its inspirations it proudly wears on its sleeve makes it clear that it's not only a remarkable love letter to a genre, but also a formidable entry…

A masterpiece that transcends homage and forges its own identity. Despite the constraints of its Game Boy-inspired art, a single burrowing mechanic weaves combat and exploration into one cohesive whole…

Mina the Hollower delivers a masterclass in classic action-adventure design, blending nostalgic Game Boy Color aesthetics with brilliant modern ideas. The world-building and secret-rich exploration are exceptional, making every discovery feel rewarding…
Mina can offer whatever challenge you're up for.
Mina the Hollower achieves the impossible by picking up the mantle of one of the most beloved independent games in recent history, while also being brave enough to diverge from the familiar path…

Mina the Hollower undoubtedly sets a new standard for what it means to be an independent game. With tributes to legendary franchises like Zelda and Castlevania and quality that Yacht Club games have honed for more than a decade, players will get much more bang for their buck with this title.

As a definitive version, I’d say it’s a lukewarm recommendation. “Dead or Alive 6: Last Round” is a good demonstration of how Koei Tecmo and Team Ninja still care about their flagship fighting franchise…
Dead or Alive 6 Last Round is a disappointment on multiple fronts: zero new features, no improvements, and, last but not least, a flawed online component…
"Great Combat... and a Late Update" Dead or Alive 6 Last Round proves that the series still boasts one of the most enjoyable and immersive combat systems in the 3D fighting game genre…
Dead or Alive 6 Last Round may not have been the upgrade we were hoping for. In its current state, not much has changed, aside from slightly improved graphics and faster load times…

DEAD OR ALIVE 6 Last Round feels like little more than a cash grab designed to sell more DLC. With no upgrade path for returning players, there is genuinely nothing here that I could recommend over DOA6…
Dead or Alive 6: Last Round doesn't redefine the series or fix all the issues it's had since its launch. However, it offers a clearly more complete experience, better graphics, and more content.

Dead or Alive 6: Last Round is a great fighting game let down by a baffling re-release strategy: no rollback netcode, no crossplay, no Tag Battle, and hundreds of euros in DLC, seven years after the original.
Dead or Alive 6 Last Round is a really good fighting game with plenty of single-player content and online features to keep newcomers and returning fans happy…

Compared to Dead or Alive 5 Last Round, which featured all previously released content and even introduced two new scenarios, characters, and a clothing destruction system, the sixth game is very disappointing in terms of content.

Dead or Alive 6 Last Round lands with its combat and maintains all that was good and not so good in the past release. While it’s hard to lambast a game you know that you can easily put hours in, even if it never stops feeling like a predatory rerelease.

Dead or Alive 6: Last Round ends up feeling like a conservative update rather than a true reinvention. You’re getting the same core game with minor additions, some visual updates, and a slightly expanded presentation layer…

DEAD OR ALIVE 6 Last Round is ultimately more of a transition than a true revival. It keeps everything that has always made the series fun: snappy combat, varied fighting styles, interactive environments, and plenty of content for solo and competitive players alike…
Dead or Alive 6: Last Round remains a solid fighter with visual upgrades, though its limited additions and outdated online play drag it down.
Dead or Alive 6 Last Round is an update to the game released in 2026. We would have liked something more impactful graphically…
Dead or Alive 6: Last Round delivers mechanically sound, fluid 3D fighting anchored by dynamic stages, but the dated PS4-era visuals, repetitive combos, and subpar netcode severely sting…
Dead or Alive 6: Last Round is, first and foremost, a repositioning exercise…

This is especially bothersome because deep down in there, the game is still just as fun as I remember. Great combat, a great roster of characters, a system that is easy to pick up, and tutorials that actually encourage you to learn the mechanics…

Last Round could have been the version of DOA 6 that fans wanted seven years ago. However, while there are some notable inclusions here, DOA 5 Last Round had an upgrade path and offered considerably more…

The main additions in DEAD OR ALIVE 6 Last Round include the five DLC characters Nyotengu, Phase 4, Momiji, Rachel, and Tamaki, bringing the roster to a total of 29 fighters, along with new costumes, new arenas, a new Photo Mode, and an overall refinement of the gameplay experience…

Dead or Alive 6 Last Round brings Dead or Alive 6 back with cleaner visuals, Photo Mode, and some former DLC fighters, and the combat is what kept pulling me back. Matches stay quick and steady, with Holds, Throws, Break Gauge decisions, and danger zones keeping rounds active…

DEAD OR ALIVE 6 Last Round doesn't revolutionize anything and doesn't make that generational leap that could have made it excellent, but it still remains one of the most important 3D fighting games in the medium.
In a vacuum, Dead or Alive 6 Last Round is a perfectly playable version of a perfectly fine fighter, but it’s still a somewhat underwhelming package all in all…
As a game in its own right, Dead or Alive 6 Last Round is simply a solid fighting game, but for seasoned players, it's not a good investment.
Dead or Alive 6: Last Round is the definitive version of the original 2019 outing, but there is no denying that the lack of new additions and modern online features is a letdown…
​Dead or Alive 6 Last Round is a frustrating rerelease. I absolutely loved it, and I wholeheartedly recommend it as a game, but I’d say exactly the same about the original release…
DEAD OR ALIVE 6 Last Round is a great game, but it has one major flaw. It isn’t a completely new title; it’s a “definitive version” of a game released seven years ago…

While there is not a lot of new content in DEAD OR ALIVE 6 Last Round, it is certainly the ‘definitive’ edition of the fighting game. It brings a few new fighters and costumes to the table, but the real eye candy is the visuals, and the buttery-smooth gameplay…

kingdom-s-return-time-eating-fruit-and-t.title: Kingdom's Return: Time-Eating Fruit and the Ancient Monster

reviews.excerpt: Not everyone will appreciate the deliberate combat in Kingdom's Return: Time-Eating Fruit and the Ancient Monster but if you go in with an open mind and learn how to effectively fight, you'll be impressed with how skillful you can dispatch your foes while emerging unscathed.

Kingdom’s Return: Time-Eating Fruit and the Ancient Monster delivers a competent action RPG with good gameplay and four unique heroes to play, each with specific moves and abilities. All this in a beautiful pixel art world…

A by-the-numbers action RPG from Inti Creates, Kingdom’s Return: Time-Eating Fruit and the Ancient Monster shows flashes of potential but is ultimately dragged down by monotonous design and shallow systems…

If you’re looking for a pixel art side-scrolling action game, you’re in luck. But if you want anything more from the experience, you could be in trouble with Kingdom’s Return: Time-Eating Fruit and the Ancient Monster.

While it has an interesting premise and a clever gimmick, it doesn't do enough with those assets to stand out among other action-platformers, including those developed by Inti Creates in years past. With that said, it's far from bad…
While Kingdom’s Return isn’t a bad game, at Inti Creates, “not bad” simply isn’t good enough.
Do you have what it takes to restore the fallen Kingdom to its former glory?

ingdom’s Return: Time-Eating Fruit and the Ancient Monster is not a bad game, the combat side should be enough to keep anyone interested for a few hours. If the game was priced at $40 to $60, I’d definitely say to avoid it, but for $15, it’s not a bad pickup for the amount of content you’ll get.
Kingdom's Return: Time-Eating Fruit and the Ancient Monster is a 2D action RPG with a management streak that does not try to dominate the scene, but to intelligently carve out its own space.
After about seven hours, I had completed all missions, so it wasn't time-consuming. The combat system is accessible and city building isn't complicated either…

The one-dimensional world, scarcity approach to strategy, and an underwhelming city-building experience make for a very lacklustre time in Kingdom’s Return. Although it has the trappings of an excellent action-strategy RPG, it is disappointing to see simplicity squander its potential.
Kingdom's Return: Time-Eating Fruit and the Ancient Monster ultimately feels torn between wanting to do too much and not enough. It brings up some interesting ideas but doesn't fully explore them…
While it may not do enough to make for a groundbreaking experience, its mix of elements has charm, though you’ll likely need to be ready to grind
I would define Kingdom's Return as a very cozy game. It's very comfortable to play, its art style is very cute, and though its soundtrack isn't that emotional, its systems are simple…

god-of-war-sons-of-sparta.title: God of War: Sons of Sparta

reviews.excerpt: Sons of Sparta delivers tight platforming and genuinely satisfying combat.

God of War: Sons of Sparta is a solid and well-crafted metroidvania with strong combat and tight level design. Within the genre, it never truly excels in any exceptional way, but it knows exactly what it wants to be…

God of War: Sons of Sparta is a well-designed, albeit conventional, Metroidvania. Combat encounters are enthralling, especially as the game progresses and enemies unleash varied attacks that demand specific methods of evasion…

Sons of Sparta feels unnecessary, a prequel few expected and one that adds little to the wider God of War saga. Still, on its own merits it’s polished and impressive, with strong mechanics, striking visuals, and standout voice work…

Sons of Sparta doesn’t reinvent the metroidvania genre, nor does it redefine God of War, but it stands as a solid choice for fans of both. The content is robust, orchestrated by high-quality art and sound direction…

Considering it takes a long time to start getting really good, God of War Sons of Sparta can test your patience but if you stick to it, you'll find one rewarding Metroidvania with oodles of content, gorgeous areas, and a solid variety of enemies and puzzles.
God of War Sons of Sparta is a solid outing that takes the franchise into a new direction while feeling a bit too safe and by the numbers for enthusiasts of the genre to truly appreciate.

Though the tonal shift might be too much for some longer term God of War vets and it really doesn't achieve anything fresh or new in the Metroidvania space, Sons of Sparta nevertheless stands as proof that AAA developers like Sony Santa Monica should continue to let talented indie devs play in…
The new God of War adventure is a solid 2D metroidvania and offers a fresh look at the early life of Kratos. However, the shift from the classic God of War style to this new approach is quite big…
Halfway through the game, I stopped comparing it to the big God of War entries and just let it be what it is; that helped a lot. Some fights could’ve hit harder…
God of War: Sons of Sparta is an entertaining metroidvania spin-off that deepens Kratos's lore through a compelling coming-of-age story and faithful genre mechanics…
God of War Sons of Sparta shines a light on a young Kratos, and to devastating effect. An emotional story carries the game…
Sons of Sparta‘s heart still beats true despite these issues. It embraces the retro aesthetic and even brings Bear McCreary back for a chiptune score…
Is God of War: Sons of Sparta a bad game? No…
Overall, God of War: Sons of Sparta is a fun Metroidvania. It captures the feel of God of War, if in a somewhat more lighthearted way than usual…

God of War: Sons of Sparta is a solid Metroidvania, but it doesn't do anything more or less than many other exponents of the genre. It works, it entertains, and it flows smoothly, but it rarely surprises…
Is God of War Sons of Sparta a good God of War game? Absolutely…

God of War: Sons of Sparta is a fun spin-off that takes a series we all know and love and places it somewhere entirely different. It's a mostly successful experiment; the Metroidvania structure works well with the franchise's mechanics, and it looks and sounds the part…
God of War Sons of Sparta has a weak start, solid middle, and strong ending. If you can get through a tedious first few hours you will eventually be rewarded with solid combat and an emotional story.

Sons of Sparta is only a partially convincing experience; it has a surprisingly well-crafted soundtrack and a simple yet enjoyable story centered on the relationship between Kratos and his brother Deimos, but it suffers from a severe lack of identity that limits its impact…
Unfortunately, the gameplay of God of War: Sons of Sparta is basic, and that's about it. The game works as a Metroidvania in the most fundamental sense of the genre…
Sons of Sparta can and will bring in fans of the IP even if they are unfamiliar with the genre in order to experience part of Kratos’ beginnings…

God of War Sons of Sparta is a Metroidvania prequel that is neither the best in its series nor the best in its genre, but it offers a story that serves to reveal a lesser-known and more humble side of Kratos…

God of War Sons of Sparta isn't a bad game, but there's almost nothing that sets it apart from the competition. It's not very pretty, the combat isn't particularly unique, and there are clumsy moments throughout…
Sons of Sparta faithfully takes elements from God of War games and mixes them with a by-the-book, sometimes too linear and clumsy metroidvania.

God of War Sons of Sparta has its merits and, within the premise of a 2D action game set in Kratos' youth, it fulfills its role in a perfunctory but satisfactory way…
God of War: Sons of Sparta is a perfectly fine Metrovania on its own, but it doesn’t live up to the Kratos lineage otherwise…

While God of War Sons of Sparta doesn't do anything special to reinvent the genre and comes with some definite unwanted baggage, it's a pretty good game that will cater more toward God of War fans than Metroidvania enthusiasts seeking the next big thing.

God of War returns to the scene suddenly, and in a form that few would have expected. Contrary to first impressions created by the setting, Sons of Sparta turns out to be quite an elaborate metroidvania-lite.

God of War Sons of Sparta offers a fresh take on the iconic action franchise that won't be everyone's cup of tea. On top of representing a significant – and undoubtedly scaled-down – departure for the beloved series, it also suffers from a slow start…

Sons of Sparta is an interesting attempt to adapt God of War into a 2D metroidvania-inspired format. The interconnected exploration of Laconia works well, and the relationship between Kratos and Deimos adds value to the narrative, revisiting the protagonist’s youth…
God of War: Sons of Sparta attempts to delve into Kratos' past with a promising narrative, but ends up betraying much of the power expected from a title in the saga…
A god of war in training, still far from his later primal power and visual impact. Even limited to two dimensions, Kratos performs quite well overall…

God of War: Sons of Sparta is a competent Metroidvania, with excellent exploration and a very well-constructed setting, but it suffers from uninspired combat, weak bosses, and a worrying number of bugs. The game has potential, but it needed much more polish to deliver on it.
God of War: Sons of Sparta is decent, entertaining, and enjoyable at times, but we should expect (and demand) much more from this franchise…
With a sea of new, genre-defining games constantly coming in, God of War: Sons of Sparta gets lost in the tide.

God of War: Sons of Sparta is a very traditional metroidvania, enjoyable for those who appreciate the genre but unable to bring anything truly compelling to the screen, as one would theoretically expect given the use of such an important intellectual property…

For the God of War completionist, there is a story incentive to play through Sons of Sparta. It builds on Kratos’ character well, shows a part of his life we have not had the chance to experience, and there is at least one small detail related to modern Kratos and his son that I am glad I learned…
God of War: Sons of Sparta stands as a metroidvania built on a solid foundation, yet it does little to distinguish itself within the genre…
Sons of Sparta should have been a slam dunk, but it just has too much holding it back to be a classic. I loved the idea; it was the execution that disappointed me…
God of War Sons of Sparta struggles to deliver on the best of God of War or the best the Metroidvania genre has to offer
Technisch unsauberes, zahmes Metroidvania-Mittelmaß. Kaum God-of-War-Flair und Balance-Probleme…

Overall this is a God of War game that fails to reach the heady heights of normal franchise levels. And while it’s an okay game, this road has been well trodden in the genre and done with more surprise and addictiveness.
Neither sacrilegious nor godly, God of War: Sons of Sparta is a pretty decent metroidvania romp…

God of War: Sons of Sparta is an incomprehensible project, whose purpose is unclear and whose overall presentation, both gameplay and narrative, fails to keep pace with both other exponents of the Metroidvania genre and the high quality that has more or less always distinguished the saga.
God of War Sons of Sparta swaps to a 2D plane to show us a glimpse of Kratos's early years.
Sons of Sparta is a pleasant character rehabilitation of a largely unlikable guy couched in a largely boring adventure about Kratos learning the value of responsibility.
God of War: Sons of Sparta isn’t a terrible game, but it’s not a more than acceptable game either. It simply sits somewhere in the middle…

God of War: Sons of Sparta might bring fans back to Greece, but it isn’t the way you expected to return. There’s a decent game when all is said and done, but it fails to materialize a unique identity from a series that has successfully rehabilitated its image…
God of War: Sons of Sparta is an underwhelming experience. I had expected more solid craftsmanship and a lot more flair from the first spinoff since 2010…
God of War Sons of Sparta takes Kratos back to his early Spartan years in a side scrolling adventure that blends exploration with heavy combat…
God of War: Sons of Sparta is a competent 2D metroidvania that expands Kratos’ past with solid combat, familiar voices, and a decent amount of content…
God of War: Sons of Sparta is a good game. The surprise release at the Sony event was a wise choice…

Sons of Sparta ends up as an uneven effort that falls short in both story and gameplay. Neither a compelling spin-off nor a satisfying side-scrolling action title, it struggles under the weight of the God of War name and never quite lives up to it.

As someone who misses the old Sony and the way they’d try weird things (and not just go for big and cinematic with every one of their games), it feels weird to criticize them for a game where they try something different. But the problem is that God of War: Sons of Sparta isn’t particularly fun…
God of War: Sons of Sparta combines valuable and human touches about Kratos' past with a new gameplay style for the series. However, it fails to deliver this gameplay in a truly innovative way…

God of War: Sons of Sparta is a respectable spin-off that expands Kratos' mythology with a charming brotherly story and solid Metroidvania bones - but it never quite reaches the heights of either the franchise or the genre it's borrowing from.

God of War: Sons of Sparta is a bog standard retro-inspired Metroidvania. There’s energetic combat and strong boss fights, though neither can quite make up for the dreary exploration and boring story, resulting in an OK experience…
Anyone expecting a faithful transition of the God of War franchise into 2D will be sorely disappointed by Sons of Sparta. It lacks the raw violence of those games and the weight behind their attacks…

The definition of mediocrity. An inoffensive but overly cautious spin-off that sticks rigidly to metroidvania conventions without stepping out of the shadow of its iconic name…

God of War: Sons of Sparta attempts to capitalize on the franchise's success with a 2D metroidvania, but largely disappoints. While it explores Kratos's past with Deimos, enriching the lore, the execution falls short…

An earnest but unnecessary God of War prequel tale told through a competent, if overly conventional, metroidvania, Sons of Sparta isn't quite a must-play. Still, it should satiate a dedicated portion of the audience until that promised trilogy remake rolls around.
A very run of the mill Metroidvania that does little of interest with the God Of War setting and stumbles in terms of the dull combat and unengaging plot.
God of War Sons of Sparta is an okay prequel—the problem is that it feels like it was released before the original 2005 game, not just taking place before it…
Sons of Sparta is a terrible God of War and a mid metroidvania. Offering something different and more modest doesn’t excuse doing things poorly…
After several hours of intense gameplay, I was incredibly excited and ultimately frustrated by God of War: Sons of Sparta. The writing lacks punch, both in terms of the characters and the story…
God of War: Sons of Sparta really does try to tackle a different approach to the series while also retaining the feel of God of War…
The most damning thing I can say about Sons of Sparta is that one day after rolling credits on it, I don’t feel anything. The game had made no lasting impressions on me, negative or positive…

God of War Sons of Sparta is not a terrible game by any means. Even in spite of all of its flaws, this is a very competent Metroidvania that will undoubtedly scratch any itch you might have to play a game in the genre…

There are things to like and even possibly love about God of War: Sons of Sparta. The combat system is smart and layered, the visual style is often beautiful, and the story eventually becomes surprisingly rich…
God of War: Sons of Sparta is a tedious and garden-variety metroidvania that brings nothing interesting to show to the class…
The Kratos we know would most likely growl in disdain. [Issue#422, p.122]

Yes, some of the gameplay gets smoother largely through repetition, but there are elements of “Sparta” that never reach beyond frustrating, including a story that’s difficult to care about, inconsistent physics, dull combat, and shallow gameplay design…
To put it simply, I just didn’t have a good time with God of War Sons of Sparta…
And yet, it’s this rather confusing mix of ideas that ends up working both for and against this newest God of War endeavour…
As Kratos' coming-of-age prequel, it's rather ironic how Sons of Sparta emulates the antithesis of his character: a Metroidvania unsure about its size, its looks, and even its own voice.

Sons of Sparta's great sin is that if you take the name "God of War" from it, it has no unique appeal to fans of 2D action-adventure games, and if you let it be called "God of War," you're more or less doing a disservice to several God of War games…

God of War: Sons of Sparta is a unique take on the God of War universe that introduces us to a different Kratos. The game is generally fun to play, but issues like the lackluster art design, low enemy variety, and a boring introduction keep it from reaching its full potential…
But I'm firmly convinced the game would be judged more favorably if it didn't carry such a prestigious name. I don't exempt myself from this…
God of War: Sons of Sparta is actually a nicely made game. Not only visually and in terms of audio…
I’m not the biggest God of War fan, but I respect and recognize the significance of this franchise to PlayStation and gaming itself…
I was beyond hyped when God of War Sons of Sparta was revealed and subsequently shadow dropped — one of my favourite franchises was being expanded upon…
As a long-time fan, I appreciate seeing the series experiment again. Not every risk needs to redefine a franchise…
I just wish it were more in tune with all of the tropes that the franchise itself had utilised all those years ago, instead of pulling from pre-existing tropes from other Metroid-Vania experiences.
A bold and respectful God of War spin-off that turns Kratos’ past into a strong metroidvania, even when its own caution holds it back.

I’m not going to sit here and tell you that God of War: Sons of Sparta is the best metroidvania ever. I’m not even going to tell you it’s the best game that I’ve played this year, because the truth is that it’s not…
Although the game provides up to thirty hours of gameplay, numerous issues make it difficult to call it a truly enjoyable experience…

God of War: Sons of Sparta lands as a disappointing spin‑off that fails to live up to the franchise’s legacy. Its repetitive gameplay, cloned enemies, limited design, and bare‑bones combat system strip away the depth and intensity that fans expect…

In a bold new direction for the series, Mega Cat Studios brings us a solid Metroidvania that centers on a narrative exploring how Sparta forged the legendary Kratos. God of War: Sons of Sparta is a bold experiment that succeeds thanks to how it expands the franchise’s lore…
God of War: Sons of Sparta Remake is a solid metroidvania with strong technical execution and engaging gameplay, though it falls short of the emotional impact and innovation of the main series.
With God of War: Sons of Sparta, Santa Monica Studio offers an interesting take on the franchise by adopting a Metroidvania structure that works well within Kratos’s universe…
You already noticed it in my review: God of War: Sons of Sparta is not a new milestone in the franchise. But it is a charming and respectful spin-off that fans will surely taste…

God of War: Sons of Sparta is a thoughtful and ambitious chapter in the series, one that reframes Kratos not as the unstoppable force he will one day become, but as a boy shaped by discipline, brotherhood, and the early challenges that would define his destiny…

As a God of War game, it lacks the scale, brutality and larger-than-life spectacle that define the series. And as a Metroidvania, it struggles to stand out in a genre that already boasts heavy hitters
God of War: Sons of Sparta is a game with clear strengths, but it fails to fully realize its potential.

God of War: Sons of Sparta is a new excursion in which you, as a player, get to explore the Greek region of Laconia as a young Kratos in a 2D Metroidvania. This colorful world and the 2D environment lend themselves perfectly to this excursion…
Kratos is back in God of War Sons of Sparta, this time on a journey into the past, in a spin-off that takes the series into the world of metroidvanias with results that aren't always positive.
The excellent animation, amazing boss fights, and the solid combat can’t save the game from being a mediocre metroidvania with the skin of God of War.

God of War: Sons of Sparta is a fun and straightforward traditional 2D Metroidvania platformer experience, covered in a God of War paint that delivers a canon but largely uneventful prequel to Kratos’ story. God of War: Sons of Sparta receives the Thumb Culture Gold Award!

God of War Sons of Sparta is polished smaller project that delivers on all fronts. The canon prequel deepens Kratos’ history, while the comat feels freat and gets better the further you get into the adventure…
God of War Sons of Sparta is a game that presents some good ideas, but rarely manages to execute them with the quality expected from a title associated with such a strong franchise…

If given a chance, God of War: Sons of Sparta proves itself to be a capable metroidvania, offering a layered combat system, an engaging quest line, and a rewarding narrative. That said, it demands patience from players, as the experience takes several hours to fully hit its stride…
God of War: Sons of Sparta does not deliver the same experience we have come to expect from the series, but that doesn’t mean it offers a shallow one…
Sons of Sparta is an interesting departure from the classic God of War games, but in terms of genre it doesn’t stand at the very top of its own pantheon.

It's not one I'd say is for hardcore fans, but it's always interesting to see big IP taken in new directions, and God of War Sons of Sparta is a good little Metroidvania that'll help fill the hole of a new entry in the series for a little longer.
God of War: Sons of Sparta turns Kratos and Deimos into the leads of a side-scrolling Metroidvania set during their Spartan training days…
God of War: Sons of Sparta proves to be a challenging, but worthy entry into the God of War franchise…

God of War: Sons of Sparta is still a great addition to the series, both as a case study and as a genre experiment. It doesn’t change God of War, but it does make it deeper by reminding players that there was once a brother behind the god and the monster, trying to do the right thing.
While I love the idea of ​​experiencing the world of God of War in other styles and genres, Sons of Sparta is somewhat disappointing…

"A unique experience in the God of War universe" God of War: Sons of Sparta offers an innovative side experience in the God of War universe, focusing on the humanity and emotional narrative of Kratos, with complex boss battles and meticulously crafted exploration…
God of War: Sons of Sparta is a good Metroidvania game. Solid, consistent, respectful…
It has some real issues as a whole, but I really enjoyed my time with God of War: Sons of Sparta. Mega Cat Studios did an admirable job translating the God of War experience into a Metroidvania…

God of War: Sons of Sparta is a bold move by Sony to diversify its offering within the God of War IP and bring in more fans (especially casual fans), but it fails to meet the quality bar most modern games are measured against…

God of War: Sons of Sparta balances ambition and restraint, limited at times but capable of offering a surprisingly human take on Kratos. Its metroidvania structure isn’t groundbreaking, yet it’s solid, with satisfying combat and a world full of secrets…

God of War: Sons of Sparta serves as a strong, mechanically solid introduction to the Metroidvania genre, competently handling all the fundamentals. However, the game ultimately falls short of being memorable, as it never attempts to innovate or push the boundaries beyond the basics.

God of War: Sons of Sparta doesn't colour outside of the lines and bring anything new to its 2D Metroidvania style, but it's a fun platformer that plays it safe and adds another layer of depth to Kratos' character.

God of War: Sons of Sparta is unfortunately neither a good God of War spin-off nor a good Metroidvania, and it also locks the otherwise appealing local multiplayer behind a generic dungeon that only becomes available after completing the main story…
God of War Sons of Sparta has a weak start, solid middle, and strong ending. If you can get through a tedious first few hours you will eventually be rewarded with solid combat and an emotional story.
