God of War: Sons of Sparta is a title that should be analysed from two perspectives: as part of the series and as a Metroidvania game…
God of War: Sons of Sparta is a strange product. It is a spin-off of a spin-off, a game that downshifts the tempo of a saga known for screaming at the top of its lungs…
God of War: Sons of Sparta works well as a prequel to Kratos’ story; however, the game stumbles on key pillars of the metroidvania genre and suffers from several technical issues.

God of War: Sons of Sparta is a very interesting prologue to the series as a whole, and a welcome return to the franchise’s original Greek setting, but as a metroidvania… I mean, it’s good, but it’s nothing I haven’t seen and played dozens of times before, especially in a post-Silksong and Prince…
Planted! is a fun and light-hearted party game that is chaotic and crazy, but it can also be frustrating, as players can win by stealing produce from other characters who put in all the work.
A trove of imaginative multiplayer ideas that has plenty of charm, but also many rough edges.
Planted! is an entertaining party game that turns vegetable farming into a chaotic competitive sport…
Planted! is, if I am being honest, forgettable…
Planted! offers creative gardening challenges and entertaining level ideas, but awkward controls hold it back

Planted! offers a fun premise and delivers the chaos expected from this type of multiplayer game, featuring attractive visuals and a lighthearted story; however, it is somewhat inconsistent, showing that it still lacks the polish needed to ensure a consistently good and enjoyable experience.
With its intuitive and chaotic multiplayer gameplay, Planted! is full of delightful nutritious fun that any couchful of chums will easily love…
Planted! delivers colourful visuals, some enjoyable multiplayer moments, and a solid core gameplay loop…
WheelMates feels like one good level for Split Fiction that was stretched into a full game for some reason. There's a strong sense of a shortage of interesting co-op activities for the RC cars.
You won't need a pen and paper to take notes as you play - unless you want to write down all the ways your partner messed things up for you. [Issue#429, p.123]
Cooperative RC car gameplay in a house full of experiments is great fun, but only if you can find a partner. The game lacks a single-player mode, which significantly limits its audience.
As a budget title of just £15.99 I have to give WheelMates some credit. It comes with a Friend’s Pass, and while it didn’t blow either myself or my co-op partner away, we did have fun…
WheelMates is certainly entertaining for a couple of evenings, but it's sorely lacking in its own unique features and falls flat compared to the other co-op games that are plentiful these days.

WheelMates is an inventive cooperative platformer set in a giant house, offering excellent level design and requiring constant collaboration between both players. However, the overall driving experience is severely undermined by the poor and unpredictable vehicle controls and a restless camera…

The Alighieri Circle: Dante’s Bloodline is a fun game, and it manages to successfully integrate creative moments with weird ones. Puzzles in this title are impressive, and the trials especially stand out as a great experience…
The Alighieri Circle: Dante's Bloodline is an adventure that demonstrates how the world of The Divine Comedy can still offer interesting ideas for the video game medium…

The Alighieri Circle: Dante's Bloodline is an old-school adventure built around a great idea: the thaumaturgical power of the writing of what is perhaps the work that represents us more than any other in the world…
The Alighieri Circle: Dante's Bloodline starts from an intriguing reinterpretation of the Divine Comedy and finds its most convincing element in the relationship between Gabriele and Delilah…

It pains me to be this harsh but The Alighieri Circle is simply not a great game. It does work from beginning to end and some of the artwork is very pretty, but the story is disappointing and the puzzles are barely worth of being called that.
The Alighieri Circle: Dante's Bloodline has some good time to offer to fans of puzzles looking for a moderate challenge…

Overall, though both narrative and puzzles are decent and the visuals are appealing, I don’t think they do enough for me. I simply wanted more—a longer experience that further explored the narrative, had more puzzles, and of course kept with having lovely visuals…
Will you manage to close the gates to hell before it's too late?
The Alighieri Circle: Dante’s Bloodline offers an intriguing blend of psychological horror, exploration and puzzles, with references to The Divine Comedy…

The Alighieri Circle: Dante's Bloodline is a brave production that shows how Italian art and literature can be a very fertile ground for the video game medium, especially when drawing on the monumental Divine Comedy…
A haunting atmosphere and impressive visuals can't save a rushed, frustrating story that fails to live up to its potential.

The Alighieri's Circle: Dante's Bloodline is a short and atmospheric walking simulator inspired by Dante's Divine Comedy. With its beautiful environments, intriguing story, exploration, and puzzle solving, the game offers a memorable journey through a visually striking interpretation of hell.

By the time the credits roll on The Alighieri Circle: Dante’s Bloodline, what lingers is less the amount of content contained within its relatively brief runtime than the sense of possibility surrounding it…

The Alighieri Circle: Dante’s Bloodline is an underwhelming experience; one that actually had a lot of potential, but is let down by a short runtime that doesn’t let the players immerse themselves in the story…

The Alighieri's Circle: Dante's Bloodlines brings a combat-free descent into Dante's Hell, with clever trials and a weird, unsettling and personal atmosphere. However, it never really gets under your skin properly.

The Alighieri Circle: Dante’s Bloodline is a fascinating tribute to the Italian poet, offering an original take on the descent into Hell through striking art direction, well-designed puzzles, and excellent Italian voice acting…
The Alighieri Circle is certainly atmospheric, but the journey was over shortly after the plot finally got interesting.

It may well be that a better-crafted story could have helped the uncomfortably short The Alighieri Circle, but given the quality of the puzzles and the weightless dialogue, not even a sermon from the pulpit could save it now…
The Alighieri Circle: Dante's Bloodline is a beautiful disappointment. Its atmosphere carries real craft, and the puzzles occasionally demand actual thought, which I appreciated more than I expected…
The Alighieri Circle: Dante’s Bloodline offers a dark and atmospheric descent into the underworld, built around challenging and varied puzzles that reward careful exploration and observation…

The Alighieri Circle: Dante's Bloodline is a successful visual and gameplay experience, driven by clever puzzles and a strikingly hellish atmosphere, but held back by a story that feels too thin and a short runtime.

I’m left with the feeling that this is a game with good ideas, but one that fails to realise its full potential. Its setting is one of its greatest strengths, particularly the design of the villa, the soundscape and the reinterpretation of Dante’s Inferno…
A stylish and atmospheric psychological thriller that trades action for clever puzzles and pure deduction…

The Alighieri Circle: Dante's Bloodline is a walking simulator with environmental puzzles that reimagines Dante's world by placing it in a new setting. Despite its strong writing and voice acting, the adventure fails to engage players due to static environments and subpar technical execution.
The Alighieri Circle: Dante’s Bloodline might fumble its storytelling, but it delivers great puzzle design that really makes it worth your attention…
The Alighieri Circle: Dante’s Bloodline stands out for its ambition and atmosphere, even if it does not quite shine with the consistency its premise truly deserves.
The Alighieri Circle: Dante’s Bloodline is a bold reinterpretation of Dante’s legacy, but in reshaping the Inferno it often loses its emotional force and unforgettable imagery…

The intent here is twofold: to spark interest through association and to provide a loose framing story. And both of these The Alighieri Circle achieves with its template drawn from the literary masterpiece…

Kejora, despite the occasional flaws that I noted, was a pleasure to experience. The story spoke to matters of protecting those around you and what you would do to ensure the safety of others, and did so in a nice, concise few hour package…
Kejora is like Stand By Me meets Groundhog Day, Studio Ghibli style, in a delightful if slightly unpolished coming-of-age Indonesian puzzle-platformer.
Kejora is an absolutely charming and ambitious indie platformer adventure that has all the necessary narrative bones for a visually compelling experience. In terms of story, it largely hits the mark…
Kejora isn’t loud. It isn’t flashy…
Kejora is a visually striking 2D puzzle adventure that leans heavily on hand-drawn, Ghibli-inspired aesthetics and a gentle, melancholic tone…
Kejora is a short and simple game with an animated art style reminiscent of Studio Ghibli films and the books I read in school to help me learn different languages…

Kejora visually draws inspiration from the works of Studio Ghibli and offers a primarily narrative-driven adventure, with few puzzles to solve and some light stealth sections. While the game is aimed at less demanding players, the overall experience feels bland and far too limited in every aspect…

The latest project from Berangin Creative is a journey worth undertaking for anyone who prioritizes the contemplation of visual art over systemic complexity, yet it demands a certain degree of indulgence regarding its sometimes timid narration and stumbling technical refinement…

For Berangin Creative’s debut game, Keejora is good first attempt. Even with the game’s problems, there’s still just enough here to make for a worthwhile playthrough, but the game’s unutilised potential brings down what could have been something quite special.
Kejora’s gorgeous art can’t mask a clunky, buggy core that feels undercooked and frustrating far more often than it is enjoyable.
Berangin Creative have set the standard for 2026 with their latest release, Kejora. Published by Soft Source Publishing, Kejora is an immersive tale of cursed magic, bravery, and forgiveness…
Truckful offers a relaxing yet occasionally tense driving experience, combining package deliveries with a mysterious story, side missions, and collectibles…

Truckful is a strange delivery game that shines in its genre mix, blending horror with cozy exploration. However, it also has plenty of speed bumps in its controls and exploration, creating a frustrating driving experience that could use more quality-of-life improvements…
Truckful‘s flow might be interrupted by frequent loading screens, but it is otherwise a pretty fun, relaxing physics-puzzle about driving through a beautiful countryside delivering packages…

Truckful has a surprisingly deep, dark story with a lot of enjoyable, entertaining characters. This carried me through the game more than I expected, and I’m glad I got to experience what it had to offer…

Truckful a game you can easily group in with titles like Dredge and Easy Delivery Co, though it relies more on physics-based safe driving. I do wish MythicOwl didn’t break up the immersion so much with the way it handles the map…
At times, Truckful feels fun, but that enjoyment wanes with repetitive objective requirements, frequent loading screens, and a just-okay story.
In the long run—much like any video game that simulates a job—Truckful turns into a routine: you end up doing the same things and, for the most part, driving the same roads…

Truckful turns something as simple as delivering packages into an entertaining adventure thanks to its physics, cargo placement, and navigation that invites you to explore the valley. Plus, the dark, Dredge-esque vibe is addictive…
Truckful is a fantastic driving adventure that hides an unexpectedly dark and mysterious heart beneath its sunny, charming visuals…
Truckful proves to be a bold experiment that stands out strongly in the indie game scene thanks to an original blend of driving simulation, inventory puzzles, and cozy horror storytelling…
In this video game, you play as a delivery driver—the only person with a vehicle in a town cut off by a strange presence lurking in the woods…

Truckful, despite its flaws, is a good alternative to traditional driving games. It has a familiar personality, with hauling physical cargo, helping a small community, exploring a remote valley, and uncovering a nefarious mystery…
For the hoarders. For the scrappers…

Truckful successfully draws players into its valley with its mysterious atmosphere and story. Its physics-based mechanics and handling capabilities make for an impressively ambitious piece of work on the mechanical front…

Truckful has lovely handling, a compelling mystery, and an opening I genuinely loved. There is a good game here, but equipment restrictions and repeated lost progress made staying in love with it much harder than it should have been.
Truckful is a delightful delivery experience that’ll offer plenty of fun across its blend of cozy and creepy driving…

Truckful surprised me with its beautiful design, fun gameplay, and a world that offers more than just a few delivery locations. Loading up, upgrading your truck, and meeting strangers combine to make for a cool experience…
Truckful is a uniquely weird physics-based delivery game blending cozy adventure with eerie thrills. Satisfying cargo packing is ultimately weighed down by clunky map navigation and UI quirks.
A mix of pointed humor, some procedural unpredictability, and what feels like a unique challenge help to at least make this an interesting experience overall.
What ultimately defines The Prisoning: Fletcher’s Quest is its willingness to lean into the messy, unpredictable chaos of its themes…

The Prisoning: Fletcher’s Quest is a great little Metroidvania, full of wacky antics and charm. Its tight controls and strong design make the journey through perilous areas a thrill, while the catchy themes linger long after the relatively short runtime…

You can’t go through half a steam store page without tripping over a Metroidvania. Lots of great experiences to be had exploring wide ranging maps with hard stop gates you can only cross once you get that next special ability…
The Prisoning is an interesting and unique game and really goes a long way to justifying the return of Acclaim. It feels familiar enough, yet sprinkling in a host of flavor to make it stand out…
Overall, The Prisoning: Fletcher’s Quest is a fun experience that’s light on the metroidvania aspects. It’s well designed and executed, if a little short…

The Prisoning: Fletcher’s Quest on Nintendo Switch is a meticulously built yet curiously lifeless micro-metroidvania, where, despite the controls being super-sharp and its pixel art vibrant, the adventure feels boxed in…
I enjoyed playing The Prisoning: Fletcher's Quest and had some laughs but its basic gameplay and small scope certainly make it feel limited.
Ultimately, The Prisoning: Fletcher’s Quest is a solid, compact experience that showcases strong fundamentals. Movement feels good, boss encounters are engaging, and the writing has a distinct voice…

The Prisoning: Fletcher's Quest isn't a bad game, and the handful of hours you'll spend with it will certainly pass the time with a decent level of enjoyment, but there isn't really anything particularly memorable here…
The Prisoning: Fletcher's Quest is exactly as it presents itself. It wants to be more, but I wish it didn't think it had to be…
Will you manage to find a way to escape from this mental prison?
I think this is a great, short Metroidvania. If you are someone who doesn’t need a well-crafted story, you just want to jump around and shoot monsters, this might be a great weekend play.
“I'd rather to play the NES version of Fester’s Quest.”
The Prisoning: Fletcher’s Quest has the bones of a good game. It features some genuinely great platforming mechanics, a weird but unhinged, visually striking opening, and entertaining core shooting…
This is a game you can easily sink a few hours into. I haven't reached the end yet, as it's quite challenging, and you certainly won't encounter the first boss in the first hour…
The Prisoning: Fletcher’s Quest isn't going to light the world on fire, but if you're looking for a platformer without any frills you may enjoy it.
The Prisoning: Fletcher’s Quest is a wild ride. It is a tight and beautiful platformer that is only held back by the randomized maps and some frustrating bosses.

Prinny Party: Going Overboard! presents a hyper-specific gameplay formula that combines strategy RPG gameplay within a co-op board game so not everyone will click with it but those who do will have an absolutely wonderful time powering-up their characters, dood.
Prinny Party: Going Overboard! has refreshing ideas and pleasant enough presentation, but the lack of a traditional online multiplayer mode really hurts its appeal…
Prinny Party: Going Overboard! is a fun and chaotic time…
While there is a solidly-designed game at the center of Prinny Party!, both the presentation and amount of content are sorely lacking for its price point…
Prinny Party: Going Overboard is a whole lot of fun with friends, but a lack of online multiplayer will make it a tough sell for many.
Prinny Party: Going Overboard! is a reimagination of Disgaea in a digital board game format.

"Prinny Party: Going Overboard!" can be a fun romp with other players as you cooperate, wheel and deal, plead, and ultimately backstab each other at the first fortuitous opportunity. It’s essentially an experiment in human psychology in game form…
It's time to give it your all and defeat the Supreme Overboard!
Prinny Party: Going Overboard! has a really interesting premise but doesn't quite provide enough material to justify its asking price…
By utterly failing to get players up to speed on pretty well anything going on, and lacking in variety, this supposed party game dives straight into the rocks
Prinny Party: Going Overboard! offers various ways to play and features a delightful array of fun events and different strategies.

Prinny Party: Going Overboard! is a meowtastic Disgaea-themed party-style RPG board game that blends chaotic gameplay with familiar series elements, delivering an entertaining experience for both solo and multiplayer…

river-city-saga-journey-to-the-west.title: River City Saga: Journey to the West

reviews.excerpt: As a roguelike, the game is naturally not designed to be completed just once…

River City Saga: Journey to the West is an accessible roguelite that charms more through its humor and personality than its depth - essentially another likeable Kunio-kun-style adventure but with a twist, though not one of its best entries.

River City Saga: Journey to the West brings together the classic Chinese myth and the Kunio games under the form of an action roguelite and as odd as that may sound, the game's comical approach, quirky visual style and immediate combat satisfaction will make players feel right at home…

River City Saga: Journey to the West’s skeletal structure should work, but the adherence to the subgenre without the knowledge of how to pare back and adapt it to this type of game makes the gameplay carry too much water with a lopsided play-to-dialogue ratio…
A very safe roguelite. It doesn't really intend to change anything, or to intrigue players with its builds…
All in all, River City Saga: Journey to the West is a flawed but fun experience. I wish the translation was better, but the combat is far more interesting than the narrative anyway.

Although I wish it had a co-op mode and more variation in its campaign, I ended up having a lot of fun with River City Saga: Journey to the West and I'm definitely looking forward to new and improved roguelike Kunio-kun games. This is a solid start…
River City Saga: Journey to the West is a fun little expedition into something different for the franchise, but it never really hit the heights I was hoping for…

Arc System Works played it a little safe with the usual roguelite difficulty curve in River City Saga: Journey to the West to avoid alienating its core Kunio-kun fanbase. Normally, that sounds like a recipe for trouble…

​Maybe it’s a mixture of burnout with the roguelike genre of late or the fact I went in expecting a fusion of two genres I really enjoyed, but River City Saga: Journey to the West just didn’t click with me…
For raw action roguelite enjoyment, there are better games for sure. As it stands, this is a solid experiment from ArcSys with a beloved franchise…

River City Saga: Journey to the West won't convert anyone who's already burned out on the roguelike formula, and it doesn't offer the mechanical depth that keeps the genre's best entries endlessly replayable across dozens of hours…
River City Saga: Journey to the West is a fun, charismatic, and solidly based roguelite beat 'em up, but it's limited in depth and ambition…

River City Saga: Journey to the West is a vibrant blend of mythology, roguelike growth, and arcade battling, and there’s enough short-term enjoyment to be enjoyed with it. It’s very colorful, and fighting is so easy that you just enjoy it without thinking much…
Available for about twenty euros depending on your support, River City Saga Journey to the West is a “small” Rogue Like friendly, easy to take in hand and pleasant to play and follow
River City Saga: Journey to the West is a curious and fun experiment that manages to reinterpret the myth of the Journey to the West through the chaos typical of Kunio-kun.

total-war-warhammer-iii-lord-of-the-end-.title: Total War: WARHAMMER III - Lord of the End Times

reviews.excerpt: Lords of the End Times is an expansion focused entirely on its protagonists, all of whom are undeniably well-realized. Thanquol is perhaps the most intriguing, thanks to his grand schemes and risk-taking nature, while Boris Todbringer answers the community’s long-standing requests…

Lords of the End Times adds a substantial amount of excellent content to an already massive game. Thanks to the new and powerful Legendary Lords and the Devastation System, Total War: Warhammer III feels fresh again…
Lord of the End Times finally brings some of the biggest fan favorites into the game—and does them justice in the process.
That said, it is clear that they do not revolutionize anything—nor do they claim to; they simply aim to add value to a game world whose core characteristics are already well-established…
Total War: Warhammer III - Lords Of The End Times might not be the final DLC of the series, but it delivers worthwhile faction updates, a strong Chaos Invasion, and a solid challenge…

Total War: Warhammer III – Señores del Fin de los Tiempos expands Immortal Empires with Nagash, the Glottkin, Boris Todbringer and Thanquol, four very different legendary lords bringing new units, heroes and mechanics that significantly change how each campaign can be approached.
Lords of the End Times works because it’s more than just a list of famous names. Nagash lives up to every bit of the hype…
One of the biggest and most ambitious DLCs ever released for Total War: Warhammer III…
Lords of the End Times can surprise you at every turn. The sheer scale of the expansion, the variety of new lords, and their unique mechanics make every campaign feel different.
Lords of the End Times is the most ambitious DLC ever seen in Total War: Warhammer III and, without a doubt, one of the most generous as well…

Total War: Warhammer III has gained four more Legendary Lords in the new Lords of the End Times DLC pack. The most prominent of them is undoubtedly Nagash and his seemingly endless army of the undead, although he is a somewhat more challenging faction to play than you may be used to…

Although some lords are way more interesting than others, “Lords of the End Times” is, overall, an amazing package that revitalizes “Total War: Warhammer III” and sets new standards for Creative Assembly — both in terms of quality and quantity. A must have for any “Warhammer” fan.

After so many years, Total War: Warhammer III reaches its conclusion with an expansion that truly feels like an event. For me, Lords of the End Times closes out one of the most ambitious trilogies ever created—not only by Creative Assembly, but in the entire history of the industry…
Fardust built a great setting here to tell more stories in this world, and the game pairs perfectly with recent deckbuilder Death Howl if you seek more not-quite-a-roguelite pastoral horror vibes…
Once you get the hang of it and a feel for how it’s meant to be played… Shards Of Order is a decent bit of fun…

Shard of Order proved to be an excellent addition to the deck-building genre. Unique in its concept, it leaves out the round and action-point mechanics found in almost every game of the genre, replacing them with the concept of time…

Shards of Order initially takes some getting used to, especially while figuring out the party roles, sprawling skill tree and the time-based combat. Stick with it though and there’s an incredibly satisfying deckbuilding RPG waiting underneath.

While Shards of Order maintains a cohesive structural path throughout its campaign, its true strength lies in how dynamically it encourages players to step out of their comfort zones and experiment with diverse strategies for every challenge they encounter…

I've had a blast with Shards of Order. I have qualms with some of the narrative presentation and would have loved to see more quality-of-life features in the overworld, but the deck-building and combat are top-notch, as is the art style and overall visual presentation…
A gloomy fantasy RPG that clearly wears its passion on its sleeve. Its creative card-based mechanics are pretty addictive, too.
Shards of Order takes the deckbuilder formula and grafts it onto a narrative-driven RPG with no roguelite structure…

Shards of Order turns time itself into the cost of every card, creating a tense and rewarding tactical RPG. Its shared deck system, striking dark-fantasy world and memorable battles outweigh the limited card variety, uneven pacing and occasional technical issues.
Shards of Order packs a lot into its short, approximately 10-hour experience, and it did more than enough to keep my attention throughout. Both gameplay and story were highlights in the early game…

Shards of Order is a really good deckbuilding RPG that tells a coherent story, has decent progression, and a battle system that challenges. This is not a game where you can just settle on your initial deck choices, but one that encourages regularly switching approaches until you break through…
Shards of Order is an excellent card-based RPG that combines deep combat mechanics with a dark fantasy setting for something genuinely captivating.

A blend of apocalyptic dark fantasy, light RPG narrative choice, and highly tactical deckbuilding that is arguably a must-play at its budget price point. Shards of Order is a striking new IP in an overstuffed genre that deserves fans’ attention and further franchise development.

Shards of Order makes a strong case for itself. It has a clear identity, an interesting combat system, a dark setting, and enough character progression to make each battle feel connected to the larger journey.
It is abundantly clear that Songs of Glimmerwick gets the cozy game genre spot on. It offers more than just a checklist of chores – a genuine sanctuary…
A lovingly crafted game brings the magic of music to every aspect of this cosy sim title. If only it increased in tempo a little sooner to unveil its delights before you get waylaid.
Songs of Glimmerwick is a lovely, inviting experience that pulls you into its world. The graphics and art style are gorgeous and perfectly match the witchy world it creates…

Songs of Glimmerwick offers a pleasant, cozy experience. It has a wide range of game mechanics, but they're a little shallow and don't quite slot together, and that cozy atmosphere risks sending you straight to sleep at times.

A beautifully soulful immersion into a world of music and everyday magic, where the worst thing that can happen to you is mice gnawing away the roots of a plant (which you can easily grow again in a day).

From side quests to class, Songs of Glimmerwick’s narrative is told in pieces. I found it felt natural to learn about the world this way, especially when you play as a witch who’s unfamiliar with the magical world…

Songs of Glimmerwick is a charming game that skillfully combines elements of magic and gardening, delivering an enjoyable gaming experience that will keep you entertained for at least 30–40 hours. Despite a few shortcomings, it's definitely a game worth giving a chance.
If you’re looking for a cosy game this autumn, and the wait for Witchbrook has you a bit annoyed, I would very much recommend checking out Songs of Glimmerwick…
In Songs of Glimmerwick, we step into a magical school where spells are learned through melodies, a mysterious island awaits exploration, and unusual characters have stories of their own to tell…

Songs of Glimmerwick is a charming magical-school RPG that replaces combat with music, exploration, gardening, and relationships. Its slower pace and occasional quest confusion may test patience, but its world and atmosphere are memorable.

Songs of Glimmerwick delivers a charming magic-school RPG built around music, exploration, gardening, and story. Its slower pace and lack of combat won't suit everyone, but the world gives you plenty to discover.
Folktales vividly tell stories that are parallel to our world to remind us of something we may have lost along the way…
This is a considered, artful game and one that’s so clearly created with love. For any fan of sewing or tactile creativity, it’s a must-play experience.
I adore Dressmaker. It is easily one of my top played games of the year…
There are a few things I would change, particularly the sewing mini-game, the repeated filtering in the emporium, and the performance issues when switching away from the game…
Wonderful cozy shop- and design-simulator, with endless opportunities for custom creations.
I have no real-world skills with sewing or dressmaking, but I thoroughly enjoyed being able to let loose creatively and make some stunning dresses…

Dressmaker feels unique among other clothing creation simulations as a result of the premise, and there are a lot of customization options. The concept feels very different than other games out there…

Dressmaker is a delightful game that can be enjoyed in short bursts or for hours at a time. The cast of characters is unique, and their interwoven storylines make the world beyond the shop feel alive…
Aandacht voor ambacht.
I had high hopes for Dressmaker, and so far it has met every expectation I have for cozy games. Cute design…
I overwhelmingly enjoyed Dressmaker during the time I had with it. This game can easily suck away hours of your day, but you will never feel like you wasted a minute.

Dressmaker is a brilliant gem of the cozy sim genre, conveying the feeling of creating a work of art as flawlessly as possible. It is a safe, calm haven for creativity to blossom, with every moment full of satisfaction and beauty.

Dressmaker has managed to impress us immensely, both for its ability to create gameplay that is both engaging and realistic, and for the stories of its characters, which never fail to capture our interest.

Dressmaker is a wonderful cozy game that offers a whole lot of gameplay for a relatively low price point. Whilst the gameplay did get a little bit repetitive for me, I can’t deny that this is a game made purely with love…

Dressmaker is comforting and addictive, the kind of game you can spend hours playing without getting tired of it, exercising your creativity and patience. One of the most interesting and unexpected surprises of the year!
I did think that I was only going to put a few hours into this game, but I can see myself coming back whenever I just want a cozy creative moment in my gameplay loop…

Dressmaker has quickly evolved from a potential-filled demo to a delightful, fully fledged game. While there are more things I’d love to see (perhaps in a future update?), it’s a wonderful play as it is, especially for the $15 price point…

It was so rewarding to shop for fun fabrics and see my vision come together on the mannequin. My only real complaint is that it would be nice to see your dresses on the characters, but overall this is a small issue that the photo mode and dress log mostly make up for.

Bigger and arguably better than its predecessor, the long-awaited Tormentum II is a welcome darkly atmospheric psychological horror sequel that will have you constantly questioning yourself, even your own perception of what is real.

The duo behind Tormentum have once again showcased their artistic talent, delivering an immersive, intriguing, and visually distinctive game that truly stands out. They’ve managed to preserve what made the first game so good while building upon it and taking things even further.

Tormentum II is a masterpiece of dark surrealism that ventures into the realm of dark fantasy, yet is rooted in existential science fiction. Eight years of hard work by the developers have resulted in a dreamlike, somber odyssey.
For all its frustrations, Tormentum II has given me plenty to chew on. Like one of its great creatures of the night, I’m not sated yet…
Tormentum II is a straightforward point-and-click adventure whose greatest strength lies in its spectacular, nightmarish art inspired by H.R. Giger and Zdzisław Beksiński…

Thinking back on my time in Tormentum II, I’m glad I swan-dived into its macabre world. As a point-and-click adventure, it wasn’t as taxing as I expected (occasionally a bad thing), and certainly not as bleak (mostly a good thing), but it still managed to surprise.
Tormentum II turns a waking nightmare into one of the most compelling puzzle adventures you'll play this year.
What we get here is a meticulously hand-drawn game with a distinctive visual style, one that truly comes into its own alongside its music. This is its main strength…

On reflection, Tormentum II is a really hard game to give a final score. I somewhat love abstract and bizarro stories, because it gives me something to mull over after, but I can understand not many people connecting with this title.
Tormentum II doesn’t need to reinvent the wheel, but it doesn’t have to. It knows exactly what made the original memorable and builds on those strengths with confidence…

Tormentum II establishes itself as a twisted, polished point-and-click adventure, capable of captivating those seeking an escape from the mundane into the unsettling realm of bio-mechanical surrealism.
If you’re looking for something to itch that relaxing scritch that you need itched, then Milki Delivery will be the nice morsel you need in your life.
It's a soothing ride with a lot of heart, taking players through a delivery cycle that is more than just a routine, but a gateway into a community that is longing to reconnect and grow once more.

Milki Delivery will provide you with a wonderfully pleasant afternoon of dairy-delivering goodness. Some slower moments feel a tad repetitive, but it’s a well-paced adventure that keeps you invested through its many upgrades and whimsical narrative…
While there are many cozy games these days, few offer the quality that you find in Milki Delivery. If you have any interest in a short and cozy experience, this is definitely a game to pick up.
Milki Delivery is a simple and cozy adventure that wins you over with its welcoming atmosphere, beautiful scenery, and the charm of its small community…
Finding a friend for the last milk cow in existence is an odd concept, but Milki Delivery is a cosy, compelling and friction-free adventure I didn't want to put down.

Milki Delivery quickly establishes a routine in a cute, friendly world, and how much you enjoy it depends on what motivates you in cozy games. It can get tedious, due to a very set rhythm to the gameplay loop…

Milki Delivery delivers a pleasant adventure for players who appreciate cozy indie games. It may not offer dozens of hours of content, but its small world has a clear identity and a heartfelt purpose.
Milki Delivery is exactly what I was hoping for – a cozy, laid-back game, with enough to explore and see and do, without ever overwhelming me with quests and timers…

Milki Delivery is a short game, but it is not a small one in spirit. Its cozy management loop, charming cast, gorgeous art style, and heartfelt story come together into something that feels genuinely special…
I’ve now played and reviewed a handful of charming, cute, and cozy games this year, probably the most I ever have in just as much time…

dragon-quest-heroes-torneko-s-mystery-du.title: Dragon Quest Heroes: Torneko's Mystery Dungeon -Classic HD

reviews.excerpt: Dragon Quest Heroes: Torneko's Mystery Dungeon -Classic HD- is almost a 1:1 port of the original Super Famicom version. The visuals were revamped, and there are a few new quality-of-life and accessibility options, but the gameplay experience is largely the same, for better or worse.

Just make sure you know what you’re getting into, because one more run may just turn into 1,000.

The game is a niche roguelike focused entirely on methodical strategy rather than fast-paced action. It comes highly recommended for fans of retro-style games looking to put their skills to the test with something akin to a large puzzle…

It’s hard not to be happy about Torneko's Mystery Dungeon finally becoming available to play on modern platforms. After all, the game is a major historical milestone for both the Dragon Quest franchise and the Mystery Dungeon series as a whole…
Dragon Quest Heroes: Torneko's Mystery Dungeon is a neat little roguelike, but I struggle to figure out how to recommend this title. For Dragon Quest fans, it's a fun little side quest to enjoy…

Dragon Quest Heroes: Torneko's Mystery Dungeon -Classic HD- revives a chapter of the franchise that is little known outside Japan, yet it settles for being a faithful reproduction of the 1993 original without taking any bold risks. The issue is that the remaster doesn't go much beyond that…
Torneko's Mystery Dungeon retains the tense, methodical appeal of classic roguelikes, with satisfying resource management and meaningful risk…
Torneko’s Mystery Dungeon -Classic HD- is a tough old-school roguelike that still knows how to keep you coming back for one more run, even when the RNG has it out for you…

Dragon Quest Heroes: Torneko’s Mystery Dungeon -Classic HD- is a fun and, above all, intriguing game. Even though I'm not a big fan of roguelikes, I quickly understood what made its formula so interesting and why Mystery Dungeon has continued to exist for so many decades…

Mystery Dungeon has moved onto greener pastures since its first outing, but much of that success was owed to a surprisingly solid first outing. Dragon Quest Heroes: Torneko’s Mystery Dungeon -Classic HD- is an alright look at its humble beginnings…

Torneko’s Mystery Dungeon -Classic HD- is at its best when every step feels like a small gamble. Its enemies, exploration, and constant curiosity about the next floor kept pulling me back, even if sluggish controls and inventory management often got in the way.

Dragon Quest Heroes: Torneko’s Mystery Dungeon -Classic HD- is the perfect way to experience the game that popularized the roguelike structure in Japan, featuring improvements that don't detract from the original experience but instead smooth out the gameplay itself.

Dragon Quest Heroes: Torneko's Mystery Dungeon may have some bumpy parts that are tough to revisit all these years of iteration later, but it serves as a pleasant enough adventure and a fascinating piece of gaming history…

Sure, it has aged poorly in a few areas, but the core gameplay remains just as entertaining more than three decades later. This charming game absolutely nails that “just one more run” feeling that every roguelike strives for, yet surprisingly few manage to perfect.

A classically styled CRPG that is welcoming to newcomers without dumbing things down, Disciples: Domination has both the gameplay and the story to keep fantasy fans enthralled for the entirety of its 40+ hour runtime.
Disciples: Domination does not upend what already works about the series. It moves Empress Avyanna’s narrative in a new direction and adds nuance and depth to all the game’s systems…
Dark fantasy RPG with highly tactical and intense turn-based combat, but weaknesses in city building and character development.
It’s difficult to fault Disciples: Domination for what it does well. The game delivers a tight tactical experience, supports a wide range of distinct factions, and offers plenty to explore…

In the end, Disciples: Domination stands in its own way and gives the impression that, although it has taken a step forward in some areas, this is offset by setbacks in others. That doesn't make it a bad game, but it's not enough to make it stand out in any way…
Although set fifteen years after Liberation, it feels almost identical in gameplay. Fans of the first entry in the rebooted series will enjoy this one as well…

Disciples: Domination offers a massive new campaign that spans anywhere between 30 and 50 hours depending on your level of difficulty and style of play, plenty of major new features with their own spin on systems and combat, baseline enhancements and QoL features that were patched into Liberation…
Disciples: Domination is a sequel that embraces absolute continuity. It corrects some of Liberation's imbalances, increases the challenge, and consolidates the foundations, but it stops there…

Disciples: Domination offers entertaining and strategic turn-based combat with loads of unit synergy to play and experiment with. Though the plot doesn’t quite deliver on its dark RPG aspirations, it’s still entertaining.

With noticeably less content and few innovations, Disciples: Domination feels more like an expansion than a full-fledged sequel. It's a decent game, nothing more, with a lackluster plot and a generic high fantasy world; a must-have for fans of Disciples: Liberation.

This is an average sequel to a tactical game, with the combat being the best aspect. Graphically, it has improved slightly compared to the last game, but the story and texts fail to attract much attention…
Disciples: Domination can feel slow, tedious, and grindy at times, but fun can still be had in its unique party recruitment mechanic and highly customizable player character…
Disciples: Domination knows exactly what it is and what it wants to do. It's an old-school strategy game with great combat but also frustratingly shallow mechanics in other areas…

Disciples: Domination is a flawed, by-the-numbers strategy RPG that shows some creativity with its units and certain boss mechanics, but lacks enough depth and variety to sustain the amount of fights it throws at you across its decently lengthy campaign…
An uninspired strategy RPG, Disciples: Domination offers an unremarkable experience that fails to stand out in a crowded genre…
Fun turn-based strategy RPG in which you must try to keep together a crumbling kingdom
Disciples: Domination is a functional but uninspired sequel that feels more like overpriced DLC than a true follow-up to Liberation…

Disciples: Domination sharpens its predecessor's strengths and adds genuine new ideas with the collision system, corpse mechanic and flexible Avyanna classes — anyone who liked Liberation will feel right at home.
Disciples: Domination is an interesting title, with solid mechanics and a well-defined identity. A convincing experience, but which would have needed extra refinement on several aspects.
Disciples: Domination serves as indirect proof that sticking to a specific setting when a series changes developers isn’t always the best approach.
One of the biggest strengths of Disciples: Domination is how it handles choices and consequences. Your decisions as a ruler matter…
I’m a huge fan of RPGs, and I particularly love an isometric viewpoint. This freedom and wide scope of vision complements the large open world…
Disciples: Domination is a good game that has its bumps in the road. With a good story and some interesting mechanics the game has a lot worth enjoying if you can get through the slow introduction.
Quote not yet available

I went into Disciples: Domination with no prior knowledge of the series and have come out the other side a fan. Its grievance and resource system builds a solid foundation for a sequel and Nevendaar and its casts of characters is a world I want to see more of…
Nitro Gen Omega captures the spirit of explosive 2000s mecha anime while delivering a surprisingly deep tactical RPG beneath its stylish presentation…

In short, this is not a video game without its rough edges; yet, it feels well-rounded and focused—built around a few highly polished and deeply explored core concepts—and, above all else, it demonstrates that potential for growth typical of those who are already doing things the right way…

NITRO GEN OMEGA from developer DESTINYbit is a unique open-world turn-based experience that offers more than expected. It’s fast, intense, and requires the player to do one helluva fun mech juggling act.
The core of the experience is an intense strategic puzzle, even if the game occasionally mumbles its instructions like a poorly dubbed transition scene…
NITRO GEN OMEGA confirms the talent and courage of DESTINYbit. The Italian studio sets aside traditional formulas to deliver a ‘handcrafted,’ brutal, and magnetic tactical RPG…
Based on a simple premise, Nitro Gen Omega’s combat is genuinely very entertaining and well thought out, and the fun animations are a nice added value…
Nitro Gen Omega manages to win you over thanks to its strongly defined identity and its ability to blend strategy and storytelling in a coherent and engaging way…
Overall I think Nitro Gen Omega is going to click deeply with a small group of players. Others who dip their toes in will probably enjoy the novelty before bouncing off to something else…

NITRO GEN OMEGA is a game about you and your Code Lyoko style crew toughing it out at the end of the world. If you enjoy turn-based anime robot action, you might find that fighting for that end is more engaging than it first appears.

Nitro Gen Omega is a game that still feels a little rough in its 1.0 release, not being as approachable in its multitude of systems as it could have been. It’s not a bad game per se, but one that demands effort to understand and pull through…
Nevertheless, the top tier teambuilding and social systems really help to push players to care for their crew and with that Nitro Gen Omega manages to rise above the little issues that I had with it.
Nitro Gen Omega was a delightful surprise in 2026, especially since the year’s midpoint hadn’t offered much for fans of this genre to celebrate.
A distinctive work, not always perfectly balanced, but with a personality so strong it's hard to ignore.
Nitro Gen Omega is an exceptional title in many ways. Immersive, polished, graphically captivating, and embodying the unmistakable style of mech-themed shonen anime…

If I had to sum up NITRO GEN OMEGA in one word, that word would be “cool”. Its effortlessly stylish aesthetics and flashy animations took me back to watching shows such as Gurren Lagann or even Megas XLR…
NITRO GEN OMEGA is a very unusual strategy RPG that will make you think outside of the box while creating emotional relationships with your teammates…
Nitro Gen Omega has elements of a deep JRPG whose mechanics are worth taking the time to master.

Nitro Gen Omega is a stylish tactical RPG with a beautiful art design, a slick UI and amazing animations. However, I can see some players being turned away by having to learn the many combat systems it throws at you, even if it’s fun once you get used to it…

Nitro Gen Omega doesn’t hide its ambitions: it wants to be a loud, loving tribute to the mecha that raised us, while still standing as a solid tactical game. And despite some repetition and a story that mostly stays in the background, it hits the mark…

NITRO GEN OMEGA is one of the most inventive strategic RPGs to hit the past few years. What appears to be a bright anime mech game at first glance turns out to be a surprisingly complex survival management RPG with profound decisions and interconnected systems.
Nitro Gen Omega is a game of wonderful strategic depth hampered by a lack of polish and a rough early progression slog…

NITRO GEN OMEGA presents a bold and highly original tactical mech concept built around time-based command planning and deep mechanical customization. Its systems offer genuine strategic depth, and the idea of assembling a personalized crew adds initial appeal…
Overall, NITRO GEN OMEGA is a solid mech tactical RPG. The combat takes a bit to get going, but it is fun and full of hyper-animated moments that look amazing…
NITRO GEN OMEGA has established itself as a tactical RPG with a very distinct identity, skillfully blending its original combat system with surprisingly deep crew management…

mafia-the-old-country-man-of-honor.title: Mafia: The Old Country - Man of Honor

reviews.excerpt: Mafia: The Old Country - Man of Honor might be more of the same, and that’s perfectly okay with me. Hangar 13’s nod to the original game is appreciated, as is the narrative flair The Old Country has already…

Mafia The Old Country Man of Honor gives fans of the base game a compelling reason to return to Sicily, delivering an engaging new story that fits seamlessly into the established narrative alongside additional activities that make its open world feel more meaningful…

Mafia: The Old Country – Man of Honor is a DLC that doesn’t aim to introduce new gameplay elements to the original game; rather, it’s more of the same, offering a narrative episode set during the main story, not after it ends…
For anyone who has finished the main campaign and is hungry for more criminal action, Man of Honor is well worth its $10 USD price tag…
Man of Honor doesn’t reinvent The Old Country, but its compact story, stronger Free Ride content and connections to the wider series make it a worthwhile return.
Man of Honor works best when it places Enzo next to a Salieri who has already learned how easily a code of honor can bend to personal ambition, creating a meaningful bridge to the first Mafia…
Cumple con las expectativas, pero te deja con ganas de más

The Man of Honor DLC expansion recognizes that Mafia stories aren't really about guns, cars or crime. They're about loyalty, ambition, betrayal and the price people are willing to pay to be part of something bigger than themselves.
2K is wrapping up content for Mafia: The Old Country with an expansion that, while shorter, is interesting for fans. It also adds an update that expands the range of activities.
Man of Honor is more of a small bonus than a major expansion, with a flat portrayal of young Salieri and a short campaign, though its low price makes the extra hours fair value.
Man of Honor is an honest expansion that lacks any real creative spark, relying almost entirely on the introduction of a young Ennio Salieri for its charm…

I don't consider Man of Honor a bad deal for those who enjoyed The Old Country and want to spend a few more hours with Enzo, Cesare, and company. For longtime Mafia fans, Salieri alone offers some intrigue…
The DLC dedicated to Ennio Salieri's origins is a natural and necessary expansion for the Mafia: Terra Madre ecosystem …

Mafia: The Old Country — Man of Honour adds some new story beats that slot in neatly into the main campaign, and it’s nice to see Sicily again after some time away. However, beyond seeing Ennio Salieri again and where the story intends to take him, it’s worth dropping back in.

It fits seamlessly into the base game's narrative—nestling gracefully between the fifth and sixth chapters of the main campaign—and offers a couple of additional chapters that can be played through in an afternoon and just as quickly forgotten.

Simply put, Mafia: The Old Country - Man of Honor is a solid expansion that doesn't do anything truly groundbreaking. The two hours of story missions are entertaining, and Salieri is a great character, while Free Ride has expanded with some pretty neat challenges and extra options…

Mafia: The Old Country – Man of Honor doesn’t breathe new life into the game, nor does it give those who maybe didn’t enjoy the initial experience a reason to return. But for everyone else, including fans of the base game and those interested in giving this a shot, I urge you to jump on board.

Man of Honor delivers a concise, well-written prequel story with strong character chemistry and satisfying Mafia fan service. Its limited campaign and frustrating stealth keep the expansion modest in scope, but expanded Free Ride activities and new weapons add welcome value for returning players.
Man of Honor proves to be an interesting addition to the game, particularly because of the way it ties into Enzo’s story while also establishing a connection to the series’ origins…
Man of Honor doesn't reinvent the wheel, but precisely for that reason, it delivers on its promises: a tight story, richer Free Ride content, and meaningful connections to the Mafia timeline.
In Sicily, women are more dangerous than shotguns, but less dangerous than knives.

Pro Jank Footy captures the cultural zeitgeist of Aussie Rules football with such charm you’d think it’s an Australian psyop. You can really feel the love for the sport in how well the actual game has been translated into this arcade-style version…
Pro Jank Footy achieves what it sets out to do by providing an affectionate, delightfully bizarre tribute to Aussie Rules…
With that sense of cheeky humour and good fun, Pro Jank Footy is a consistent blast. It’s not the deepest game, but it certainly is one of the most funny I’ve played this year…

Pro Jank Footy's simplicity is in some ways to its detriment, but the sheer slapstick spectacle of the thing, and the clear reverence for the pixelated sports games of old carry it to greatness. This isn't the sort of thing I'd play on the regular, but it is absolutely coming out at group events.
An absurd take on Australian Rules Football inspired by retro arcade sports games of the past, Pro Jank Footy never really finds its footing.

Pro Jank Footy is a tremendous mess of a game, and I mean that in the most complimentary way possible. It boils down a complicated sport into its purest, fundamental arcade form before breaking it through a chaotic overloading of its simple systems…
Over-the-top roguelite arcade comedy sports game
It may not always play fair, and it certainly doesn't take itself seriously, but that's exactly what makes Pro Jank Footy such an entertaining surprise.

It might not be the Aussie Rules simulation that people want, but Pro Jank Footy is an accessible sports game, that ended up making me appreciate some of the finer points of the real sport. Perfect for beginners that have no idea about this sport, or any sports for that matter.
While I had high hopes that this wild and crazy take on sports could channel some old-school Mutant League vibes, I’m wishing perhaps they’d stopped the jank at mere amateur status…

Pro Jank Footy is far from the deepest experience out there, but it simply nails the spirit of the sport, along with a fresh burst of Aussie humour, so much so that it’s really hard not to enjoy on some level.
I enjoyed Pro Jank Footy, but it isn’t the deepest sports game. Furthermore, the sense of randomness and the often challenging action make it a frustrating title…

Pro Jank Footy is a blast in short bursts, especially when competing with friends and family. The wild possibilities escalate as more goals are kicked, creating moments of pure anarchy dabbled with nostalgia for anyone familiar with the sport in its best era…

The true hilarity (and often frustration) comes if you play with mates in local VS. I suspect this fun would also apply to the future online mode, but I do wonder however how much lag will impact the experience…
Roman Sands RE:Build is a bizarre, captivating psychological experience that transforms mundane service work into a surreal exploration of routine, survival, and identity…
A frenetic tale of two realities, both alike in dysfunction, which immerses the player in servitude and struggle.
Roman Sands RE:Build is a strange game, and I mean that as a compliment. Its repetitive work can become a real obstacle, but the atmosphere, mystery, music, and unusual characters kept me invested…

I’m glad I got to see the story through, however, with its not-so-subtle homages to the likes of Danganronpa and Evangelion. It remains one step away from its mysteries and doesn’t take them to extreme lengths…
It’s the type of game that folds your brain over on itself, constantly making you question your reality and see the world around you from countless angles.

More of an experience in nature than your classical videogame, but they stick in my brain nonetheless. I've been waiting for this game since its announcement and now that it's here, it's something I'll be thinking about for a long while…
Undoubtedly one of the more unusual games I’ve played running this site, it may have some appeal for the right crowd, but it definitely will take patience to see everything it has to offer

Roman Sands RE:Build is a wonderfully bizarre adventure that blends surreal apocalyptic storytelling, dark satire, memorable characters, and striking vaporwave aesthetics with an outstanding jungle and breakcore soundtrack…
Arbitrary Metric and Serenity Forge invite us to play the role of a hotel bellhop under unusual circumstances.
Roman Sands RE:Build was the first narrative title of 2026 to intrigue me, primarily because it recognizes that the defining feature of games as a storytelling medium is gameplay, not text…
Roman Sands RE:Build is one of those games that is easier to experience than to explain, and it arrives today with a personality that has become increasingly rare in the indie landscape.

It’s pretty much “just” the music and bosses I have issues with, the game otherwise works quite well, is extremely well-polished, outside of the otherwise uncharacteristic framerate issue with the fourth stage, as on-rails shooters tend to be!
Wild Blue Skies reminds me why arcade shooters were so much fun. It blends the best bits of on-rails action and Saturday morning cartoons into something nostalgic without feeling dated…

Wild Blue Skies shines when it deviates from the Star Fox formula with some truly phenomenal missions. But its lacklustre story and presentation, and a reluctance to truly step out of Star Fox’s shadow holds it back.
Wild Blue Skies is a solid homage to Star Fox 64 overall. It's visuals are fantastic and it's gameplay controls well and is fun overall…

Overall, Wild Blue Skies is a charming, budget-friendly tribute to classic Star Fox that delivers plenty of arcade replayability, colorful locales, and stellar voice work for a modest $15 price point…
Wild Blue Skies is a tribute to the legendary Star Fox. Its inspirations are clear, from its similar protagonist and crew to the level design and structure…
Wild Blue Skies was a bittersweet experience for me…
Wild Blue Skies treads an extremely fine line between being an homage to Starfox and a blatant copy of it…
Wild Blue Skies is a game that teeters between homage and plagiarism. It could almost be described as a reskin of Star Fox, as it closely mirrors its story, gameplay, and progression…
It looks fantastic and has a great presentation, but with archaic game design and mediocre combat, this Star Fox clone fails to properly get off the ground.

Wild Blue Skies captures that classic Star Fox charm at a budget price, but lacks the refinement that made Nintendo’s classic so memorable. The often-unfair gameplay can frustrate, yet there’s still some old-school fun to be had for the right price.
Games don't get much less innovative than Wild Blue Skies but there's no denying that it's a solidly-made game so that's cool, I guess.
Wild Blue Skies is mechanically fine. It’s as tepid as you could possibly get for an on-rails shooter…

Bowie and pals’ adventure successfully impersonates the Star Fox 64 experience, but it’s an underwhelming impression. Nostalgic moments and satisfying action appear occasionally, but it pays homage to a fault and doesn’t find space to present its own personality…

Wild Blue Skies tries to imitate the classic Starfox formula, but only with middling success. The flying is ok, but issues with difficulty, repetitive arcade structure, and virtually no narrative to keep you wanting to play, it is reduced to a score chaser.
On-rails shooter Wild Blue Skies looks quite nice, but it's extremely derivative of Star Fox, and pales in comparison in just about every way.
With a lack of individuality, Wild Blue Skies forced me to make comparisons in which it lost out almost every time.
Wild Blue Skies is a decent rail shooter when it finds the courage to be itself, but too often it’s simply Star Fox 64 But Worse – worse flying, worse story, worse difficulty tuning.

Wild Blue Skies is what happens when a spiritual successor takes too much inspiration from its predecessor. There is nothing inherently wrong with the game, but if you have played Star Fox 64, or the remake, you have played Wild Blue Skies…

Wild Blue Skies showed a lot of promise, and I was super excited to get my hands on it, especially with all the recent fervor over Star Fox. Rail shooters are a great time, and this particular brand of rail shooter really lends itself well to having fun at different levels of play, across many runs…
Wild Blue Skies falls way short of the mark, making every attempt capture Star Fox 64's spirit without taking any risk to be original in its own right.
Wild Blue Skies works extremely well as a homage to Star Fox 64. Its old-school approach is refreshing at a time when so many other games are trying to put their own spin on the formula…
While Wild Blue Skies proudly wears its on-rails inspiration on its sleeve, this adventure with the Blue Bombers is well worth taking flight.
The Blue Bombers make for a fantastic squadron, and I can't wait to suit up and fly with my new comrades again soon.
So, is Wild Blue Skies worth your time and attention? For the price, I’d say so…

I’m someone that has no real nostalgia or love for Star Fox 64, but Wild Blue Skies is such a pale imitation of that game. This is especially true when a fully remade Star Fox just got released two months ago, it’s hard to find any reason to play this over that…

It’s a wonderful thing to see games made with such love and admiration for what came before them. Wild Blue Skies proudly wears its love for Star Fox 64, and for the most part, this is a charming homage to a legendary video game…
Wild Blue Skies looks the part, but shallow design, its barebones story, and noticeable technical issues leave this on‑rails shooter struggling to stay airborne.

Wild Blue Skies is a shoot ’em up game that successfully updated itself for modern platforms, bringing stylish and beautiful graphics along with gameplay that truly satisfies once you master its moderate learning curve.
Wild Blue Skies is a fun and nostalgic trip that successfully scratches that retro rail-shooter itch, even IF there are some areas of its design that feel a little lacking…
Wild Blue Skies delivers a Star Fox experience you have most likely already played. If you haven't, then you get a game that performs and controls well, and is fun…
“Wild Blue Skies is a joyful love letter to Star Fox 64, delivering fast-paced rail-shooter action, precise controls and imaginative space battles that capture the spirit of the classic…
Wild Blue Skies does a great job of recreating and innovating on classic 90's on-rail space shooters. The design throughout is excellent and the gameplay is tight and engaging.

I’ll admit, Wild Blue Skies would’ve been a more interesting release had it launched before the Switch 2 remake of Star Fox 64, or if that game had never existed. Yes, it feels like Star Fox 64 with the world’s most elaborate find-and-replace function applied to it…

Wild Blue Skies delivers fast-paced aerial action, colorful cel-shaded visuals, and an energetic retro soundtrack. However, it carries sparse environments, bullet-spongey enemies, and strong resemblance to Star Fox keep this flight from reaching greater heights…

Chuhai Labs understands the fundamentals of what makes games in this genre tick. Even lacking polish in some small, key areas, if you're hungry for an on-rails shooter I can see this briefly satiating the hunger.
Despite its flaws and strengths, Wild Blue Skies is a good choice for rail shooter lovers and for Star Fox fans who don't own a Nintendo console to relive the nostalgia…
I spent a lot of time pointing out the things I did not like about Wild Blue Skies, but that does not mean I think it is a bad game. Nothing that I mentioned is unrecoverable…

A wonderfully deep (ha!) puzzle detective game, Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss treads a fantastic line of respecting the source material, updating it in a fresh way, and delivering some deliciously restrained horror.

Despite a minor hiccup with a save issue, the overall polish and responsiveness from the developers leave a strong impression. For players who enjoy narrative- driven investigations with psychological depth, this is a journey well worth taking.
Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss is, crashes and caveats aside, an excellent game. Key is a triumph, the puzzles are imaginative, and the final chapter earns everything it demands of you…

Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss is a first-person 3D investigative horror adventure strongly focused on exploration. Gameplay revolves around collecting clues, reading documents, and solving environmental puzzles, with the combination of scanner and sonar helping to mitigate classic pixel hunting…
Big Bad Wolf's Lovecraftian investigation horror experience pulls out all the stops to corrupt the brains of many a Cthulhu fan. From dazzling locations full of references to volumes of H.P…

Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss has a lot to offer for those looking for an immersive, narrative-driven horror thriller. Its gameplay doesn’t demand quick reflexes or wanton destruction, but rather deduction skills and attention to detail…
Its puzzles may leave something to be desired, but Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss legitimately feels like one of Lovecraft’s dark stories experienced first-hand.
Big Bad Wolf's latest is a visually arresting Lovecraftian deep-dive that prioritizes "big brains" over big guns, but its overly safe structure prevents it from reaching true horror greatness…
Derin delilik.

Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss certainly nails its Lovecraftian atmosphere, especially in some truly daunting set pieces. Its environmental puzzles are also well implemented, offering a high level of challenge that fans of the genre will appreciate…
Rather than delivering a consistently smooth experience, Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss is a game that thrives in its investigation systems, atmosphere, and environmental storytelling…
Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss is an ambitiously detailed Lovecraftian detective story that makes great use of its supernatural horror source material
Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss is an interesting take on the Cthulhu Mythos, even if its overall narrative doesn't stand out…

Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss is an incredibly fun adventure puzzle game with some very well put-together mechanics that make investigating and solving puzzles almost as interesting as its Lovecraftian roots, which is why it's a shame that it fumbles properly connecting those roots to its gameplay,…

At times innovative and, above all, immersive, Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss offers a solid experience for a mystery game, but it sorely lacks the horror element that’s supposed to send shivers down your spine.

A game that isn’t afraid to let players muddle through it on their own is an idea to be lauded, and here there is a core mystery that will provide a compelling enough reason to continue if you can get into the rhythm of the puzzling.
In the end, Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss is fine. The lack of combat combined with a lack of guidance creates a challenging and refreshing experience for most — and frustrating for some…
Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss is a Lovecraftian game to the core, but it is also an investigative adventure with an overly slow pace and less frightening than expected.
Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss takes an ambitious swing but it just doesn’t fully connect. It nails the atmosphere and tone but struggles where it matters most…
Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss is an interesting AA detective game, with fun investigation mechanics and a gripping premise, but quickly falls apart in the second half of the story…

When The Cosmic Abyss plays more like a walking sim or a first-person horror, it's excellent story really shines through, but its overdesigned systems tend to get in the way of its otherworldly ambitions. [Issue#424, p.119]

It's a horror game that isn't scary, an adventure game that isn't exciting, and a narrative-driven game that feels more like a glorified tech demo. There's nothing bad to be found here, but nothing worth writing home over either.
Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss is not the most successful experiment. The reimagining of the walking simulator's core principles did not go as planned.
Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss is a flawed, but interesting experience. The narrative is straight out of a Lovecraft story and it escalates into a suitably maddening conclusion…

The Cosmic Abyss suffers from an overly long and exhausting plot, a forgettable and frankly unnecessary villain, a stamina system that felt tacked on more than anything else, and an empty, boring world. I wanted to like this game, but the negatives heavily outweigh the good…

There is a general paucity of Lovecraftian thrills in this puzzle adventure, and as much as I try not to resent a game for the crime of simply being bad, Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss is a frustratingly fragile waste of time and energy that I will never get back…
Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss is the monotony of desk work, and the drudgery of reading pages of emails after your morning cup of coffee.

Ultimately, the game did make me lose my sanity, but not always for the reasons I expected. While the atmosphere is great, the lack of technical polish in the latter half of the game is a significant hurdle…

As a relative noob to Cthulhu’s lore, I really loved Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss because of its more psychological horror nature. It would be easy to make this into a monster blasting, shooter type but the choice to slow things down, and tell a more methodical story was a great thing…

Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss does ample justice to its grim source material, fashioning a compelling investigative adventure which generously drips with atmosphere but one which is sadly somewhat undercut by a wealth of technical issues that take the sheen otherwise what is a highly enjoyable…
Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss can't find anything interesting or new to say about Lovecraft's work, but its detective adventure gameplay is an extremely promising foundation.
What lurks deep in the ocean? Really deep, past all the weird fish and that…

Cthulu: The Cosmic Abyss wraps an intricate puzzle game in the shell of a beautifully designed, if familiar, Lovecraftian atmospheric horror experience that strikes a delicate balance between allowing you to solve problems on your own and consistently propelling you forward.

Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss revels in the player working to unravel the unfathomable in Lovecraft's influential universes. This is a game about eerie atmosphere and piecing together mysteries, taking players on a claustrophobic journey through infinite horrors.
Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss has some interesting ideas, but it hides them behind poorly explained puzzles and deceptively linear design.
The kind of cosmic horror that makes you ponder your place in the universe
While there are many games based on the works of H.P. Lovecraft, Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss stands out thanks to its focus on you conducting an investigation…
H.P. Lovecraft’s work still has legions of devoted fans, including within the gaming community…
Cthulhu: The Cosmic Abyss is a bold, atmospheric horror story, but frustrating puzzles and a double-edged sanity system leave it too unpolished to fully convince.

stalker-2-heart-of-chornobyl-cost-of-hop.title: S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chornobyl - Cost of Hope

reviews.excerpt: If you haven’t played S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2, ‘Cost of Hope’ marks the perfect time to jump in…
S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2 returns to the Zone with The Price of Hope and, above all, an "Update 2.0" that significantly refines the experience…

STALKER 2's Cost of Hope expansion represents the next generation of a beloved franchise, but this time, it sets the stage for the most major evolution we've ever seen. It's a haunting, emotional, and twisting expansion that might not be perfect, but comes damn close.

Stalker 2 has received its first major expansion—as well as its biggest update to date—and the game is moving in a very positive direction. The foundation was solid at launch, but through successive fixes, improvements, and new content, it is increasingly becoming the game it was always meant to be.

An almost perfect story DLC, even if I have to grit my teeth a little.

I persisted in spite of the horrors, because the rest of what’s on offer in Cost of Hope is so stellar and well worth picking up.
S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2 has finally been tidied up enough.

I’m left feeling thoroughly satisfied with this grand new addition to a game I already loved…
